title: From bad to worse: customer mistreatment and service sabotage across encounters
abstract: Purpose Customer mistreatment is a significant issue in both practical and academic contexts, especially in the service industry. Drawing on the stressor–emotion model, this study aims to use a sequential two-encounter field design to test the lagged effects of customer mistreatment on service sabotage at Time 1 and Time 2. The study also explores the moderating effects of personal controls (i.e. conscientiousness and emotional stability) and situational control (empowerment) on the above relationships. Design/methodology/approach The analytical sample consisted of 190 frontline employees matched with 380 customer evaluations across two consecutive service encounters. Data were gathered in multiple stages: frontline employees first completed questionnaires on demographics and personal traits, and then, immediately after service encounters. This procedure was repeated for a subsequent service encounter with a second customer to capture multiple interactions for each employee. Findings The findings indicate that emotional exhaustion mediates the relationship between customer mistreatment and service sabotage at both Time 1 and Time 2. Furthermore, empowerment weakens the positive relationship between customer mistreatment and emotional exhaustion, whereas conscientiousness and emotional stability attenuate the indirect effect of customer mistreatment on service sabotage through emotional exhaustion. Practical implications The findings underscore the importance of safeguarding frontline employees from the detrimental effects of customer mistreatment. Hospitality managers should foster employee empowerment and provide adequate organizational support to help employees cope with demanding customer interactions. At the same time, managers should recognize conscientiousness and emotional stability as valuable personal resources that may buffer the effects of emotional exhaustion and reduce the risk of subsequent service sabotage. By integrating these organizational and individual-level approaches, hospitality organizations can mitigate the adverse spillover of customer mistreatment across successive service encounters and, ultimately, preserve service quality. Originality/value This study advances understanding of boundary conditions by simultaneously examining individual traits and an organizational factor. The findings reveal that conscientiousness and emotional stability significantly buffer the indirect effects of mistreatment through emotional exhaustion, whereas empowerment primarily mitigates the direct impact of mistreatment on exhaustion but does not alter the exhaustion–sabotage pathway. By integrating temporal dynamics, emotional processes and multilevel moderators, this research provides a more comprehensive and realistic account of how customer mistreatment unfolds in frontline service contexts.

title: Too little time, too much to do: how time poverty undermines employees’ proactive service behavior
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the relationship between time poverty and hotel employees’ proactive service behavior by identifying future self-continuity as a mediator and competitive climate as a moderator. Design/methodology/approach This research uses a multimethod design to test the hypotheses. Study 1 uses a recall-based experiment with 220 hotel employees to establish causality. Study 2 draws on a two-wave field survey of 298 employees from five hotels in China to enhance ecological validity and test the boundary conditions. Findings The findings reveal that time poverty significantly undermines hotel employees’ proactive service behavior, thereby establishing the mediating role of future self-continuity. Furthermore, competitive climate moderates this effect such that the indirect negative effect becomes stronger when competitive climate is high. Practical implications This study helps hotel managers understand the impact of time poverty on employees and offers practical guidance for monitoring and alleviating it through employee-centered scheduling, workload redistribution and protected time, thereby sustaining employees’ proactive service behavior. Originality/value This study examines hospitality employees’ time poverty by shifting attention from the tourists’ temporal experiences, which have dominated prior research, to employees’ chronic scarcity. Moving beyond the affective and cognitive reactions emphasized in earlier studies, it reveals an identity-based mechanism grounded in self-control theory. It further identifies competitive climate as an organizational boundary condition that managers can redesign or reduce to contain the behavioral costs of time poverty.

title: Fueling service initiative: how AI assimilation shapes employees' proactive service behavior through AI crafting
abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping how employees engage in service work. However, few studies have examined how AI assimilation (i.e. the extent to which AI technology is integrated and routinized in work activities and processes) affects employees' proactive behaviors. This study investigates how the breadth and depth of AI assimilation shape proactive service behavior, examines the mediating roles of approach and avoidance AI crafting, and tests job autonomy as a moderator. It further examines whether employees exhibit higher proactive service behavior when these two crafting strategies are used in a more balanced way. Design/methodology/approach Based on Conservation Of Resources (COR) theory, this study uses paired-sample survey data from 234 employee-manager pairs in China's service industry. Stepwise regression, polynomial regression, and response surface analysis are applied to test the hypotheses. Findings The results show that both the depth and breadth of AI assimilation positively influence proactive service behavior. Approach AI crafting mediates both relationships, while avoidance AI crafting only mediates the relationship between the breadth of AI assimilation and proactive service behavior. Employees exhibit the highest level of proactive service behavior when using both crafting strategies in balance, indicating that approach and avoidance AI crafting are complementary. Furthermore, job autonomy strengthens the positive effect of AI assimilation on approach AI crafting, while weakening its positive effect on avoidance AI crafting. Originality/value This study advances service operations management research by shifting attention from AI adoption to AI assimilation and specifying the mechanism through which AI assimilation shapes frontline employees' proactive service behavior. It also challenges the traditional dichotomous view in job crafting by proposing that approach and avoidance AI crafting may be complementary.

title: Organic copper substitution mitigates feed-derived copper emissions by enhancing bioefficacy and redox–microbiota homeostasis in Eriocheir sinensis
Stereodivergent telomerization of linear functionalized dienes with amines
abstract: Despite the importance of divergent synthesis to obtain different isomers for medicinal and material chemistry, divergent stereocontrol over four distinct selectivity factors remains a fundamental challenge. The telomerization reaction is limited to the transformation of simple unfunctionalized 1,3-dienes to circumvent intractable stereoisomeric mixtures. Here we report an orthogonal telomerization platform using linear functionalized 1,3-dienes as the substrates, which simultaneously dictates regio-, geometric, diastereo-, and enantioselectivities. Diverse types of γ-amino esters are prepared from identical, readily available unsaturated esters and amines via synergistic palladium and acid catalysis, with each precisely obtained out of hundreds of potential telomers. Several chiral phosphoramidite ligands have been developed to promote the transformation. This study showcases the potential of multidimensional stereo-manipulation for the industrially valuable telomerization reaction.

title: Verification makes discovery matter
Antiferroelectric hafnia down to the 2D limit
abstract: Antiferroelectricity is a material property characterized by alternating electric dipoles spontaneously ordered in antiparallel directions. Antiferroelectrics are promising for energy storage, solid-state cooling, and memory technologies; however, these materials are scarce, and their scalability remains largely unexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that single-crystalline hafnia, a lead-free CMOS-compatible material, exhibits antiferroelectricity under compressive-strain conditions. We observe antiparallel sublattice polarization and stable double-hysteresis in single-crystalline (111)-oriented epitaxial La-doped hafnia films grown on yttrium-stabilized zirconia and show that the antipolar orthorhombic phase of hafnia adheres to the Kittel model of antiferroelectricity. Notably, compressive strain strengthens the orthorhombic order in thinner La-doped hafnia films, achieving a very high ordering temperature of 850°C in the two-dimensional limit, highlighting hafnia’s potential for advanced antiferroelectric devices.

title: In-cell structures visualize human pre-ribosome assembly in the nucleolus
abstract: In eukaryotes, ribosome biogenesis initiates within the nucleolus, a hallmark multilayered compartment of the nucleus. Structures of pre-ribosomes have been characterized ex situ, but their assembly pathways within human nucleoli have not been described. Here, we used cryogenic correlative light and electron tomography to visualize molecular landscapes within HeLa cell nucleoli and obtained in-cell structural snapshots of both ribosomal subunit precursors, the SSU processome and the pre-60S. These recapitulate major states resolved previously ex situ and reveal additional critical interaction partners, including the RNA exosome, rixosome, and nuclear export receptor CRM1-RanGTP. We further show how pre-ribosome assembly landscapes are altered upon RNA polymerase I inhibition. Our study combines molecular structures with cellular context to elucidate the spatiotemporal assembly pathway of the human ribosome.

title: Targeting an atypical G protein–coupled receptor signaling pathway for cardiac fibrosis therapy
abstract: Cardiac fibrosis independently predicts adverse outcomes in heart failure (HF), yet no Food and Drug Administration–approved therapy directly targets fibrotic remodeling in the heart. To address this unmet clinical need, we used a multidimensional drug discovery pipeline centered on a human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)–based platform. Through high-throughput screening, we identified CGS15943 (CGS) as the lead antifibrotic compound and validated its activity in human cardiac fibroblasts, three-dimensional engineered heart tissues, and animal models of HF. Mechanistic studies revealed an atypical adenosine receptor (AR)–dependent signaling pathway in which AR subtypes converge on Gβγ (the βγ subunits of heterotrimeric GTP-binding proteins) to activate phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)–AKT and yes-associated protein (YAP). CGS suppressed this signaling axis, thereby reducing fibrotic gene expression and fibroblast activation. These findings establish AR-driven Gβγ signaling as a potential therapeutic target for cardiac fibrosis.

title: Neural evidence that dogs segment the speech they hear with a humanlike consonant bias
abstract: Across many human languages, consonants carry more lexical information than vowels. During speech segmentation, humans, unlike nonhuman primates, rely more on consonant than vowel patterns, despite vowels’ greater acoustic saliency. To investigate whether this consonant bias is specific to humans or could also emerge in other species exposed to human speech, we performed noninvasive electroencephalography in humans and dogs. Intertrial coherence measures of neural entrainment and event-related potentials revealed enhanced word-level tracking for consonant- compared with vowel-structured streams in both species. This suggests that dogs, similar to humans, exhibit consonant bias when segmenting the speech they hear. Linguistic regularity–based processing biases can thus also emerge in a nonspeaking species exposed to speech.

title: Hedging El Niño isn’t the same as adapting to it
abstract: Record-setting warm waters slosh eastward across the tropical Pacific, forming El Niño. This recurrent climate pattern reconfigures severe weather worldwide, and with it, the global economy. Scientists have forecast El Niño for decades, but never one this strong. Financial markets are responding rationally, minimizing their exposure in the regions most at risk. But hedging is not the same as adapting. At best, its dollar logic obscures El Niño’s human costs, and at worst, it pulls capital from the very places that need investment most.

title: Embracing triplet nitrenes for C-to-N replacement of complex bicyclic (hetero)aryl azides
abstract: Despite recent proof-of-concept advances, aromatic carbon-to-nitrogen replacement reactions remain substrate specific and exhibit an overreliance on harsh oxidation methods that preclude their deployment in demanding contexts. Transformations relying on singlet nitrene valence isomerization, in particular, have suffered from competitive intersystem crossing to the triplet spin state, which does not undergo the same rearrangement. In this work, we report a reaction that productively engages triplet aryl nitrenes for carbon-to-nitrogen replacement on the benzenoid ring of a range of bicyclic heteroarenes, including naphthalenes, anthracene, indoles, benzofurans, benzothiophene, indazoles, and benzisothiazoles. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions, which enables its application to complex, sensitive natural products.

title: Ancient introgression drives wild boar expansion and phenotypic diversification of domestic pigs
abstract: Despite the ubiquity of wild boar populations across Eurasia, their origins, routes of dispersal, and phenotypic evolution remain uncertain. Here, using 745 genomes representing populations across Eurasia, we demonstrate that wild boar expanded from South Asia during the Middle Pleistocene. This expansion was preceded by a Pliocene introgression (~3 to 5 million years ago) in South Asia from an archaic Suinae lineage that introduced a ~43 megabase X-chromosomal haplotype into the ancestral wild boar population. This haplotype includes loci associated with increased body size and adaptation to cold climates. During domestication, this region was selected at least three times independently to develop modern large-bodied breeds. Our findings reveal a long-lasting evolutionary legacy of this ancient introgression, which provided genetic material that was later shaped by natural and artificial selection.

title: Escape of the BC200 gene to a human poxvirus reveals its persistent transposition in primates
abstract: Transposable elements mobilize within and occasionally between genomes, including from host to virus. We identified two insertions of the human BC200 noncoding RNA gene in the poxvirus molluscum contagiosum virus (MCV), which were likely acquired through long interspersed nuclear element 1 (LINE-1 or L1)–mediated retrotransposition during modern human history. Although BC200 was co-opted approximately 40 million years ago to regulate neuronal translation, we show that it never lost its mobilization capacity. Rather, BC200 functioned as a “master” source of L1-mediated germline retrotransposition events throughout anthropoid evolution, spawning hundreds of lineage-specific insertions. Additionally, BC200 has produced insertion polymorphisms segregating in the human population, including individual-specific insertions indicative of ongoing transposition activity. Thus, BC200 blurs the line between gene and transposon, combining stable function with persistent mobilization, including a recent escape into a human poxvirus.

title: Fibroblasts restrain gut inflammation by IGF1-dependent regulation of innate lymphocytes
abstract: Fibroblasts exhibit phenotypic and functional heterogeneity in chronic inflammatory diseases, but how these changes impact immune outcomes remains poorly understood. We identified that a fibroblast population expressing insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) was reduced in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Using mouse models of intestinal inflammation, we found cross-talk between IGF1-expressing fibroblasts and group 3 innate lymphoid cells (ILC3s). IGF1 stimulation limited the ability of ILC3s to produce C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 10 (CXCL10) and recruit plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) to restrain gut inflammation. We propose that this regulatory pathway is conserved in human ILC3s but may become impaired in IBD. Our results define that anti-inflammatory fibroblasts safeguard the gut through regulation of an innate lymphocyte–pDC axis.

title: Mammals produce cyclo -octasulfur to suppress lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis
abstract: Elemental sulfur is an evolutionarily ancient metabolite, yet its generation, storage, and function in animals have remained unclear. We show that mammals harbor elemental sulfur in the form of its most stable allotrope, cyclo -octasulfur (S 8 ). We found that S 8 accumulates to millimolar concentrations in mitochondrial membranes and in lipid droplets in both mouse and human cells. We further identified lipid droplet–associated nitric oxide synthase as a source of S 8 biosynthesis and found that S 8 accumulation in lipid droplets limits lipid peroxidation and suppresses ferroptosis. Accordingly, intra-articular injection of solubilized S 8 reduces lipid peroxidation in a mouse model of osteoarthritis. Together, these findings reveal an endogenous pool of S 8 in mammals that may protect cells from oxidative membrane damage by modulating cellular sensitivity to ferroptosis.

title: An in-body networking system for communication between wearable and implantable therapeutics
abstract: Networks of bioelectronic sensors and actuators enable closed-loop therapies that connect distant, related physiological dynamics. Currently, device interactions are limited by communication methods that inefficiently penetrate tissue and require bulky components. Inspired by the ionic signaling of the nervous system, we engineered a communication platform that uses tissue as a conductive medium to transmit signals among implants and wearables through epidermal, subcutaneous, intraperitoneal, and gastrointestinal spaces. Devices generate transient electric fields that selectively activate other devices when receiving pulses that switch on their specific transistor circuits. Implants are syringe-injectable, require negligible power consumption in listening states, and provide >10× greater tissue communication coverage than Bluetooth. In vivo in rats, we demonstrate coordinated, full-body networks of sensors and neural interfaces that enable wireless dual-limb motor control.

title: Conformal oxides decouple chemical stability and energetics at NiO x /perovskite interfaces
abstract: Nickel oxide (NiO x ) is a common hole transport layer (HTL) in perovskite photovoltaics, but the chemical reactivity of NiOx surfaces accelerates degradation when contacting perovskites. We developed an ultrathin, conformal tin oxide (SnO x ) interlayer to suppress interfacial reactivity between NiO x and perovskite. SnO x is typically an electron transport layer, but we show that the energy alignment can be modified for hole extraction using molecules with dipoles. This synergy yielded high efficiency in perovskite photovoltaic devices and showed an ~10x improvement in T 90 lifetime in open-circuit conditions under AM1.5G at 65°C. This structure also improves resilience to thermomechanical durability, as minimodules retained 95.7% of their initial performance after 1000 thermal cycles (−65° to 85°C), highlighting the importance of interfaces for robust perovskite photovoltaic modules.

title: How 8 years of social and individual learning interact to shape ecological competence in orangutans
abstract: Cultural learning permeates human skill and knowledge acquisition. To understand its importance for nonhuman apes, we analyzed just under 7000 records of behavioral bouts of social and individual learning across wild orangutans’ 8-year dependency period to assess their combined effects on ecological competence, which is crucial for independent survival. Social learning was five times more frequent than individual learning and influenced subsequent learning for hours. Immature orangutans varied substantially in their learning propensities, and those with heightened social and individual learning propensities developed the most expansive diet profiles at independence. Furthermore, social learning had a compensatory effect on diet profile development when individual learning was low. Our findings advance the science of cultural evolution by showing how multiyear social and individual learning interact to shape great apes’ broad ecological competence.

title: 2D theoretically twistable material database
abstract: The study of twisted two-dimensional (2D) materials, in which twisting layers create moiré superlattices, has created opportunities for investigating topological phases and strongly correlated physics. The broader potential of a seemingly infinite set of twistable 2D materials remains largely unexplored. Here, we define “theoretically twistable materials” as single- or multilayer structures that allow for the construction of simple continuum models of their moiré structures. Our high-throughput algorithm systematically searches for theoretically twistable semimetals and insulators based on the Topological 2D Materials Database (2D-TQCDB). By analyzing key electronic properties, we identify thousands of candidate materials, propose representative twistable materials, and provide examples of crystal growth and exfoliation for several of them. Our results provide a resource for future experimental and theoretical studies of moiré systems.

title: Ceramide synthesis mediates colorectal cancer metastasis through a YAP-driven regenerative program
abstract: Mechanisms by which primary tumor cells acquire metastatic capability through metabolic and signaling adaptations are currently poorly understood. We demonstrate that tumor-intrinsic ceramide metabolism, amplified by dietary fat, initiates colorectal cancer metastasis. We observed that dietary fat exposure triggers a sustained increase in de novo ceramide biosynthesis, mediated by the dihydroceramide desaturase Degs1 . Ceramide accumulation activates yes-associated protein (YAP) through protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A)–mediated dephosphorylation, promoting a durable shift toward a distinct YAP-driven regenerative (YAP-DR) program, marked by Basp1 , that promotes metastasis. Selective elimination of Basp1 high cancer cells prevented metastatic seeding. Degs1 loss reduced ceramide levels, YAP activity, YAP-DR signatures, and metastasis without affecting primary tumor growth, whereas blocking ceramide degradation enhanced YAP activity and metastasis. These findings identify ceramide-induced YAP signaling as a key mediator of metastatic initiation, operating independently of primary tumor expansion.

title: Senescence-directed nanotherapy ameliorates fibrosis and overcomes immune exclusion in cancer
abstract: Fibrotic remodeling of tissues and tumors establishes immunosuppressive microenvironments that drive organ dysfunction and, in cancer, limit response to immunotherapy. Senescent-like cells are conserved drivers of fibrosis and therapeutic targets, yet their functional heterogeneity complicates therapeutic intervention. Here, we show that P-selectin is expressed by a subset of senescent-like cells in fibrotic tissues and tumors. Leveraging fucoidan-based nanoparticles that bind P-selectin, we developed senescence-modulating nanoparticles (SMNPs) to selectively target these disease-associated states. SMNPs exerted potent antifibrotic and immunomodulatory effects while improving the therapeutic index. Mechanistically, we identified a pathogenic, immunosuppressive macrophage population as a functional target in vivo. In fibrotic tumors, niche remodeling restored immune infiltration and sensitized tumors to immune checkpoint–based therapies. These findings establish SMNPs as a generalizable strategy to target pathogenic senescent cell subsets across fibrosis and cancer.

title: Science still has expertise; what it’s lost is authority
abstract: In the years since the pandemic and the political turmoil surrounding the American scientific establishment, much time has been spent discussing why science has lost influence on public policy in the United States. A time when scientific advice about vaccination, nutrition, and environmental regulation was more readily heeded seems a distant memory. Scientific expertise has been decoupled from a sense of authority and standing to dictate policy on matters ranging from public health to climate change. The explanations for this separation include the rise of technologies like the internet and artificial intelligence, mistakes made by scientists and scientific institutions, and weaponization of anti-science ideas by political actors. But what if there’s a larger historical trend that suggests the disconnect between expertise and authority was inevitable? A new idea in philosophy called the “unicontext” suggests that the advance of technology, along with basic human desires, has been leading to this point for the past century.

title: Unlocking cycle life of lithium metal batteries
abstract: Lithium-ion Coulombic efficiency (Li CE) is widely used to evaluate interfacial stability and predict cycle life in lithium-ion batteries but fails in lithium-metal batteries (LMBs), in which higher Li CE does not reliably lead to longer cycle life. Here, we reveal that electrolyte depletion caused by unstable solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) leads to electrolyte dry-out and induces lithium compensation through anode-to-cathode cross-talk, whereby soluble anionic species formed at the anode migrate to the cathode and release Li + from electrolyte salts upon oxidation. We establish quantitative relationships among SEI quality, electrolyte consumption, and lithium compensation, enabling accurate cycle life prediction. The SEI quality–based framework derives quantitative guidelines for electrolyte design to extend electrolyte lifetime and sustain long cycle life in high-energy LMBs under ultra-lean electrolyte conditions.

title: Prussian blue regulates ion dynamics in perovskite solar cells
abstract: Perovskite photovoltaics are limited by structural instabilities initiated during crystallization and amplified under operation. We report that a lattice-matched Prussian blue scaffold directs heterogeneous nucleation to produce highly oriented, strain-relaxed films. Its redox-active Fe–C≡N–Fe network mediates the conversion of Pb 0 and I 0 defects, and its rigid open framework suppresses A-site cation redistribution and the resulting electronic inhomogeneity under bias. This strategy yielded champion power conversion efficiencies of 26.1% (n-i-p) and 26.9% (p-i-n; 26.2% certified), scaling to 23.4% in 6-centimeter–by–6-centimeter minimodules and a certified 22.9% in 30-centimeter–by–30-centimeter submodules. Submodules with initial power conversion efficiencies ranging from 20.2 to 21.0% showed robust durability under accelerated aging and no discernible decline relative to a silicon reference over 5 months of outdoor testing.

title: Two-dimensional topological quantum chemistry and catalog of topological materials
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) topological materials host symmetry-protected, disorder-robust edge states central to quantum technologies. Yet they remain scarce compared with their 3D counterparts. We adapted the topological quantum chemistry formalism to layer groups and studied the band topology of 8872 entries from the computational materials databases C2DB and MC2D. We found 4073 topological or obstructed entries, including 905 topological insulators and 1003 obstructed atomic insulators, greatly expanding the library of such materials in two dimensions. Detailed electronic and topological properties of all materials have been compiled into a Topological 2D Materials Database (2D-TQCDB), and the edge states of selected new materials have been studied in detail. Our methodology has been implemented in publicly available programs, designed to study the topology of any nonmagnetic monolayer or multilayer material.

Bankruptcy lawyers and credit recovery
abstract: I study how bankruptcy law firm advertisements affect household credit, exploiting the borders of local TV advertisement media markets. I document a significant advertising effect on filing rates and subsequently show that ad exposure is associated with better financial outcomes. I then characterize how ad-induced filers are different from existing filers in terms of case, financial, and credit variables. I find that ad-induced filers are more likely to receive a discharge, file with lawyer representation, and be first-time filers. I interpret these findings as evidence that bankruptcy law firm advertisements help mitigate frictions in the bankruptcy decision.

title: Information access and college admission outcomes
Long-term impacts of youth mentoring and therapy: Experimental evidence from Chicago
abstract: We conduct a large-scale, randomized controlled trial of a six-month intervention combining intensive mentoring and group cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for youth in Chicago, following study participants for up to five years. The program was designed to engage young people at higher risk of involvement with the criminal justice system, and successfully did so with a take-up rate of 62%. Participants averaged 177 hours with mentors and nine hours of group CBT. After 24 months, youth offered the program experienced a 19% reduction in the probability of being arrested. Notably, this impact persists into adulthood, as effects remain stable through five years post-randomization. A reduction in arrests for violent offenses is driving this overall arrest reduction, with a 23% reduction in the probability of a violent-crime arrest after 24 months. The program does not impact school enrollment persistence (graduation or being enrolled), but shows suggestive improvements in school behavior and school mobility. We conclude that programs that combine mentoring and CBT can serve as a model for engaging a harder-to-reach population of youth, and can be effective in reducing criminal justice contact in the longer run.

title: Transporting behavioral insights to low-income households: A field experiment on energy efficiency investments
abstract: Established behavioral insights may not generalize when applied to under-represented target populations. Iterative approaches that identify such external validity failures to guide policy deployment at scale and to inform subsequent design refinements gain importance. We implement this approach in a field experiment involving 1800 low-income households in one of the largest energy efficiency assistance programs. Despite extensive co-designed vetting, most behavioral insights proved ineffective or inefficient. Notably, loss-framed interventions backfired by reducing take-up. We rank insights by their Marginal Value of Public Funds (MVPF), identifying ‘unexpected winners’ that outperform alternatives rated as promising by experts and laypeople. Our analysis suggests that factors specific to low-income households, such as scarcity, fundamentally alter behavioral responses, necessitating guided deployment to optimize future public assistance design.

title: Robust estimation and inference for high-dimensional panel data models
abstract: This paper provides the relevant literature with a complete toolkit for conducting robust estimation and inference about the parameters of interest involved in a high-dimensional panel data framework. Specifically, (1) we allow for non-Gaussian, serially and cross-sectionally correlated and heteroskedastic error processes, (2) we develop an estimation method for high-dimensional long-run covariance matrix using a thresholded estimator, (3) we also allow for the number of regressors to grow faster than the sample size. Methodologically and technically, we develop two Nagaev--types of concentration inequalities: one for a partial sum and the other for a quadratic form, subject to a set of easily verifiable conditions. Leveraging these two inequalities, we derive a non-asymptotic bound for the LASSO estimator, achieve asymptotic normality via the node-wise LASSO regression, and establish a sharp convergence rate for the thresholded heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent (HAC) estimator. We demonstrate the practical relevance of these theoretical results by investigating a high-dimensional panel data model with interactive effects. Moreover, we conduct extensive numerical studies using simulated and real data examples.

title: Markets of Pain: Opium, Capitalism, and the Global History of PainkillersBenjamin RobertSiegel, (Oxford University Press, 2026. Pp. 368. ISBN 9780197527825. Hbk £26)
abstract: This book argues that the story of opioids in modern world history did not begin with the American OxyContin crisis of the 1990s, and that this story cannot be told entirely as one of prohibition, crime, and smuggling.The core of the book is a narrative of the attempts of the Ottoman, Turkish, and Indian governments to negotiate a role for their opium growing and processing sectors in an international system that tried to restrict opiates to 'legitimate' channels, especially after the system was dominated by the Americans after World War II.This requires the author to draw on sources from several archives and touch on aspects of scientific, diplomatic, economic, social, and political history.It is also a surprisingly personal history.Siegel follows Ottoman opium brokers, St. Louis chemists, Indian bureaucrats, Turkish politicians, American drug crusaders, and others whose individual stories enliven the narrative whilst also showing how the drug business remained contingent and based on ethical factors and local relationships no matter how much governments tried to turn it into a fully rational, bureaucratic, and marketized system.Turkey, and its chief rival, India, had long histories as producers of opium.Prior to 1945, India sent much of its production to the colonial opium monopolies of Asia (not discussed in this book), and Turkey was the chief supplier of raw opium to the European dominated pharmaceutical industry.In each place, governments had been working to impose greater legibility and control on their systems, both to guarantee profits and to ensure the emerging international drug control system, exemplified by the 1925 Geneva Opium Convention, that their production was not being diverted into illicit channels.After 1945, the United States became the dominant producer and consumer of medical opioids and also the dominant power in the international drug control system.A system of managed trade developed, with India and Turkey title: The power to price: pricing regimes and governance of the cobalt global production network
Political Connections, Financial Constraints, and Corporate Taxation
abstract: Abstract We find that the effect of political connections on tax planning depends on firms’ financial conditions. After increased political connections, financially unconstrained firms increase tax planning and spending on tax services, as documented in prior studies, whereas constrained firms decrease tax planning and spending on tax services. Moreover, decreases in tax planning are only present for constrained firms that obtain new bank loans and public debt and when the connected politicians serve on banking-related committees. Our results suggest that by facilitating access to external financing, political connections reduce financially constrained firms’ use of tax planning as an internal financing tool.
journal_name: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis

title: Connected Social Media
abstract: Abstract We examine whether and how firms use connected social media outlets to counteract negative coverage in traditional media. Employing a sample of Chinese listed firms with ties to social media outlets, we find that connected outlets portray firms more favorably than unconnected ones. Following unfavorable coverage in traditional media, connected outlets shift attention toward long-term prospects and promote favorable narratives, consistent with an optimism-shifting mechanism. The effect is more pronounced when firms have stronger incentives to stabilize stock prices and when managers face heightened career concerns. Our findings highlight the role of connected social media outlets in shaping corporate narratives.
journal_name: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis

title: On the Value of Improved Forecasting for Specialty Crop Producers Through Intra‐Season Supply Allocations
abstract: ABSTRACT How to manage harvest and storage of agricultural products has been one of the long‐lasting questions in agricultural economics. We study the value of improved forecast accuracy for the producers in the context of intra‐seasonal supply allocation, particularly for specialty crops with multiple harvest cycles within a season. We first explore how the forecast accuracy affects intra‐seasonal storage decisions. We then derive the expression for the marginal value of the improved forecast accuracy and show that the gains from the improvement in the forecast accuracy occur by shifting the optimal storage choices to those under certainty (i.e., the state is revealed) from those under uncertainty. Finally, we provide numerical illustrations on how the value of the improved forecast accuracy for the producers differs across different degrees of market power showing that relative gains from the improvement are larger when the market is more competitive. We conclude by drawing broader implications highlighting the importance of the interaction among information, storage and market structure.

title: Early career effects of entering the labor market during higher education expansion
abstract: Abstract We evaluate the labor market effects of an increasing supply of high-skilled labor, resulting from a higher education expansion at established German universities. Exploiting variation in exposure across regions and cohorts, we estimate early career effects for labor market entrants. We find that high-skilled wages decline initially, particularly in non-graduate jobs, but recover over the first 5 years of experience. For graduate job takers, we even report positive wage effects after 5 years. We explain the dynamics of the effects by the interplay of several mechanisms: immediate supply effects, recovery through regional mobility, and increased productivity of graduate jobs.

title: The value of a statistical life year
abstract: Abstract Embedded in the value of a statistical life (VSL) is a stream of valuations of each expected year of life. The value of a statistical life year (VSLY) has a policy-relevant role analogous to the VSL, except that it monetizes risks to short periods of life extension. This article reviews previous studies and reports new labor market estimates of the average VSLY and the variation of these values with age using two methods—inferring the average VSLY based on estimates of the VSL and a new method that provides direct empirical estimates of the valuation of a discounted life year. The direct estimates of the VSLY yield larger values than the constructed estimates. The VSLY based on fatality rates by industry and occupation is $600,000 to $800,000 at a 3% interest rate. Estimates based on age-adjusted fatality rates are somewhat lower. The discount rate used in assessing the VSLY has a pivotal effect on the estimated VSLY. The VSLY is substantially lower in the absence of discounting and more than doubled at a discount rate of 10%. Failure to use a positive discount rate greatly understates the VSLY. The article also reviews previous VSLY studies as well as estimates of the discount rate for years of life expectancy.

title: Modelling the macroeconomic impact of Brazil's ecological transformation plan: a stock-flow consistent approach
abstract: In 2023, the Brazilian government launched the Ecological Transformation Plan (ETP), a new development strategy aimed at promoting environmentally sustainable economic growth while enhancing productivity and social equity. This paper evaluates the macroeconomic impacts of the ETP's financial policy mix, by developing a stock-flow consistent model. The analysis focuses on representing the policy mix embedded in the ETP—particularly its financial instruments—and evaluating its implications for investment, growth, and macroeconomic stability. A key contribution of the paper is the explicit modelling of financing mechanisms designed to mitigate currency risk, a structural constraint that affects many EMDEs and limits the scalability of low-carbon investments. By incorporating these features into an SFC framework, the paper provides new insights into how financial structures and policy interventions interact with real economic dynamics. Simulations through 2030 indicate that the ETP is expansionary, with projected GDP growth rising up to 1.6% and the creation of 360,000 to 900,000 new jobs. While the plan improves the primary fiscal balance by increasing tax revenues, it introduces specific trade-offs: the reduction in unemployment may prompt the Central Bank to raise the Selic rate to curb inflation, and increased demand for capital goods is expected to widen the current account deficit by 0.2–0.4 p.p. of GDP.

title: From Algorithmic Trading to Generative AI: Artificial Intelligence, Systemic Risk, and the Transformation of Financial Markets
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence can improve financial information processing while also synchronizing decisions, concentrating operational dependence, and accelerating market feedback. Yet evidence on these effects is divided among market microstructure, machine‐learning risk analytics, algorithmic intermediation, and generative AI. We integrate these literatures using 769 English‐language articles, reviews, and book chapters retrieved from OpenAlex for 1990– July 29, 2026, bibliometric performance and relational analyses, and structured content coding of 96 studies. Publication growth accelerated after 2021, but collaboration remained fragmented and the 2023–2026 frontier shifted sharply toward generative AI and governance. Bibliographic‐coupling assignments were stable to stricter thresholds and the exclusion of partial‐year 2026 records, although weak cluster separation cautions against treating algorithmic communities as theories. Content synthesis shows that automation usually improves normal‐state liquidity and signal extraction; systemic risk emerges when common models, objectives, infrastructures, or narratives correlate actions and meet thin risk‐bearing capacity. Evidence is strongest for average market‐quality effects and weakest for vendor‐commonality, agent autonomy, and equilibrium feedback. We propose an architecture–use–amplifier–outcome framework and ten falsifiable designs for identifying when AI creates resilience rather than scalable fragility.

title: The Evolving Role of Finance in Environmental Strategy: Integrating Climate, Sustainable, and Biodiversity Finance
abstract: ABSTRACT The literature on climate finance, sustainable finance, and biodiversity finance has expanded rapidly over the past two decades, yet it remains conceptually fragmented and often organized around specific mechanisms, risks, or policy initiatives. This paper provides a systematic and integrative review of this evolving field by combining bibliometric, thematic, and qualitative analyses of 1228 peer‐reviewed articles published between 2007 and 2025. The results document a progressive broadening of research focus, from climate‐related risk pricing and disclosure, to firm‐level sustainability strategies, and more recently to natural capital and ecosystem‐oriented financial mechanisms. Building on these patterns, the paper introduces the strategic integration pathway of Climate, Sustainable, and Biodiversity Finance (CSBF), a conceptual framework that organizes the literature around three dominant and coexisting logics of financial–managerial engagement: defensive, strategic, and regenerative. Rather than treating these domains as sequential stages or isolated subfields, the framework highlights increasing depth of integration between finance, management, and environmental systems. By clarifying how the role of finance evolves under tightening ecological constraints, the study contributes to theory development in sustainable finance and provides a structured foundation for future research, managerial decision‐making, and policy design.

title: The Visible Hand, the Invisible Hand, and the Firm's Own Hand What Propels ESG Engagement in Chinese Companies
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper surveys the empirical literature on the antecedents of corporate environmental, social and governance (ESG) engagement in China, distinguishing substantive ESG actions, ESG disclosure, externally assigned ESG performance, and symbolic or reputational responses. Synthesizing 126 studies published between 2004 and 2024 in leading journals on the UTD, FT and ABS lists, we develop a tripartite analytical model in which forces at the government, market and firm levels jointly determine ESG behavior through three interaction logics, namely mutual reinforcement, substitution and contingency. The evidence identifies regulatory pressure, policy incentives, state ownership and political connections, together with media scrutiny, product market competition, institutional investors and customer demands, as well as organizational resources, governance arrangements and strategic orientation, as the principal antecedents of ESG engagement. Their relative importance varies systematically over time and across regions, industries, and ownership types, although changes in research attention do not by themselves establish a transition in Chinese ESG governance. We further document considerable theoretical fragmentation, as institutional, stakeholder, and resource‐based perspectives are widely applied but seldom combined. The survey concludes with an agenda for future research covering meta‐analytic validation, firm‐level mechanisms, heterogeneity across ESG dimensions, digitalization and cross‐country comparison.

title: A Bibliometric Review of Digital Currency Research: An International Perspective
abstract: ABSTRACT Drawing on the Web of Science database, this study reviews the digital currency papers published between 2016 and 2025. Using bibliometric analysis, we document a substantial increase in research output in this field, reflecting growing academic and policy interest. The United States and China emerge as the two most productive countries in digital currency research, with China taking a leading position in publication volume after the launch of its central bank digital currency (CBDC) in 2019. The leading journals publishing digital currency research are Finance Research Letters , International Review of Financial Analysis , and Economics Letters . The most extensively studied topics include Bitcoin price dynamics, the risk‐return characteristics of digital currencies, and CBDC development. Building on our bibliometric evidence, we further identify several avenues for future research, including corporate finance and governance, financial intermediation, financial inclusion, digital currency ecosystem and financial stability.

title: Identification of Relationship Lending in Bank–Borrower Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT Relationship lending refers to lending based on close bank–borrower relationships, expected to increase credit availability and support real economic activity. This paper proposes the ST‐B filter, a novel framework identifying significant ties in temporal bipartite networks. Applying our method to Japanese financial data (1977–2021), relationship lending comprises about 10%–35% of total lending and is associated with 33% larger loan volume than transaction lending. Our method uniquely enables the analysis of relationship lending using only transaction data, without requiring detailed information on bank–borrower relationships.
journal_name: Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics

title: Can we be serious? A comment on Mata on genre
abstract: There are many lenses through which to analyze the history of economics, the number growing with scholars’ increasingly expansive conceptions of the field over the last few decades. This article offers a brief and affirmative comment on Tiago Mata’s discussion of the use of the concept of genres in history of economics and its application to the study of works that fall under the heading of “popular economics.” Thinking in terms of genre—which draws us to questions of form, style, and purpose—offers a useful vantage point from which to explore the history of economics, one that encourages us to think in a different set of ways about what is being done and how and why, and the implications for understanding the history of economics.
journal_name: The European Journal of the History of Economic Thought

title: Generative Search: Evidence from a Large-Scale Field Experiment
abstract: Generative search is an emerging search paradigm that integrates Generative AI (GenAI) into traditional search engines by presenting users with AI-generated responses before conventional search results. Whereas keyword-based search requires consumers to translate their underlying needs into effective keyword queries, generative search lets users express those intentions directly in natural language, a shift made possible by GenAI’s new mode of information presentation. This shift moves the consumer-search engine interaction upstream to the stage of problem formulation, rendering empirically observable a previously hidden phase of search behavior: the mapping from problem formulation to keyword articulation. Yet, it remains empirically unknown whether generative search increases consumer purchases and how search behavior changes when it can begin from expressed intent rather than keywords. Using a large-scale field experiment conducted on Meituan, a leading Chinese technology platform, this paper provides empirical evidence on the effectiveness of generative search. We find that generative search significantly increases consumer purchases. Further analysis reveals that generative search facilitates more effective and diverse keyword queries and reduces exploratory browsing and clicking, while concentrating evaluation within relevant categories and merchants. The empirical evidence is most consistent with a mechanism in which AI-generated answers provide information about consumers’ underlying needs, while also expanding awareness of relevant attributes and shifting attention toward more relevant categories. These findings provide empirical insights for future consumer search models that allow search to originate at the intention-expressing stage. This paper was accepted by Raphael Thomadsen, marketing. Funding: Financial support from the Ministry of Education – Singapore [Grant A-8001730-00-00] is gratefully acknowledged. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.02458 .

title: Policy‐Level Environmental Architecture and Corporate Renewable‐Energy Transition
abstract: ABSTRACT Corporate renewable‐energy transition is often assessed through climate commitments, ESG scores, or carbon indicators, although these measures may not reveal firms' capacity to translate formal policies into operational change. Using a newly assembled point‐in‐time panel of European listed companies drawn from the STOXX universe over 2015–2025, this study constructs a holistic environmental‐management architecture score comprising resource/nature and climate/energy management pillars. The common estimation samples contain 1161 firm‐year observations from 264 firms for the 1‐year horizon and 869 observations from 215 firms for the 2‐year horizon. Firm and fiscal‐year fixed‐effects models relate environmental‐management architecture in fiscal year to subsequent changes in renewable‐energy use over and , complemented by pillar‐level and component‐level decompositions, alternative fixed‐effects structures, and sector exclusions. The holistic architecture score is positive but imprecisely estimated. Resource/nature management is positively associated with subsequent renewable‐energy improvement at both horizons, whereas climate/energy formalization is not. Water‐efficiency policy is marginally significant at the 1‐year horizon and statistically significant at the 2‐year horizon. The findings show that formal environmental policies do not carry uniform information about operational transition and highlight the value of examining policy domains and implementation‐related organizational routines separately.

title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Gender Diversity at the Innovation Core and Environmental Innovation
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper estimates the effect of gender diversity on firm‐level environmental innovation. We use a large Spanish panel data and construct an inverse‐covariance‐weighted environmental innovation index. Identification comes from persistent within‐firm increases in women's representation, measured relative to a 2‐year rolling pre‐event baseline. Across several difference‐in‐differences estimators, a 5% increase in women's share of in‐house R&D personnel is associated with an increase in environmental innovation of 1.2–1.6 points. This corresponds to approximately 3%–4% of the sample mean and builds gradually over the years, consistent with a durable reorientation of innovation effort rather than a transient compositional change. The corresponding evidence for the overall female employment share is weaker and estimator‐sensitive. Empirical Bayes analysis shows that firms with larger internal underrepresentation of women in R&D have lower environmental innovation. The evidence suggests that the relevant margin is not simply gender diversity in the firm, but gender diversity inside the innovation‐producing core.

title: Generative AI Disclosure in Advertising: From Intent- to Production-Based Disclosure
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming advertising production and introducing new forms of disclosure at the point of exposure. Existing research treats disclosure primarily as a cue signaling persuasive intent, yet GenAI disclosures increasingly communicate how content was produced rather than why it was created. This paper reconceptualizes disclosure in AI-mediated advertising by positioning GenAI disclosure as a signal of production conditions. Integrating signaling theory, source credibility theory, the persuasion knowledge model, and the heuristic–systematic model, the paper develops a conceptual framework that differentiates declarative, regulatory, and infrastructural disclosure as distinct rendering conditions. The framework proposes that GenAI disclosure influences consumer evaluations through two complementary inferential pathways: perceived source attribution and production-based agent knowledge, defined as consumers’ beliefs about how persuasive content was generated and what those production processes imply for evaluating the persuasion agent. It further specifies how consumers’ motivation and ability shape the likelihood of heuristic versus systematic processing. The paper advances advertising theory by explaining how disclosure operates when its primary referent shifts from persuasive intent to production conditions and by providing a framework for understanding why similar disclosure cues may generate divergent evaluative responses across consumers, contexts, and forms of GenAI use.

title: Should Ads Be Assertive? A Meta-Analytic Review of the Effects of Assertive Language on Perceived Freedom Threat, State Reactance, and Persuasion Outcomes
abstract: Advertising messages often use assertive language to capture consumer attention and drive behavioral compliance, yet empirical evidence for its effectiveness remains inconclusive and contradictory across studies and contexts. This meta-analytic review synthesized 142 samples examining the effects of assertive language in advertising messages on perceived freedom threat, state reactance, and persuasion outcomes. Drawing on psychological reactance theory, we used meta-analytic structural equation modeling (MASEM) to conduct the first test in the reactance literature of a serial mediation model in which assertive language first increases perceived freedom threat, which subsequently heightens state reactance, ultimately reducing persuasive effectiveness. Overall, assertive language significantly increased perceived freedom threat (d = 0.72) and state reactance (d = 0.39), while demonstrating a small but significant negative effect on persuasion outcomes (d = −0.08). Importantly, MASEM provided evidence that the effect of assertive language on persuasion outcomes was serially mediated through perceived threat to freedom and state reactance. Moderation analyses revealed that advertising domain significantly moderated the effect on state reactance, with nonprofit contexts eliciting stronger reactance responses than for-profit contexts. These findings clarify the mechanism of psychological reactance in advertising and provide clear guidance for advertisers on when and why to avoid assertive language.

title: Income inequality and entrepreneurial motivations: A cross-country analysis of the moderating roles of trade openness and individual capital
How firms bundle R&D and marketing capabilities for innovation: a systematic review and contingency model
abstract: Purpose This study systematically reviews 25 years of research on the R&D–marketing strategy nexus (2000–2025) and proposes a contingency model explaining when and why specific capability configurations enhance innovation performance. Design/methodology/approach We identified 140 peer-reviewed studies through a PRISMA-compliant search of Scopus, filtered by the ABS Academic Journal Guide. Each study was coded using the Antecedents–Decisions–Outcomes/Theories–Contexts–Methods (ADO-TCM) framework. Bibliometric mapping and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modelling complemented the deductive coding with inductive identification of thematic clusters. A co-word robustness check validated the LDA solution. Findings Marketing capability, network relationships and technology capability rank as the most frequently studied antecedents, with organisational structure and environmental dynamism close behind; market orientation, which earlier work placed at the centre, is coded in fewer than one study in ten. Marketing-strategy and product-development decisions dominate the corpus almost equally, while temporal sequencing of orchestration choices remains unstudied. Two in five studies invoke no explicit theory; evidence concentrates in the USA and East Asia and in manufacturing or multi-industry samples, with services almost absent. Integrating ADO–TCM patterns with LDA clusters, we derive three testable propositions: a turbulence–agility mechanism, a digital–complementarity mechanism and a legitimacy–consistency mechanism. We introduce the concept of integration intelligence, the meta-capability through which managers diagnose which orchestration configuration fits their current competitive context. Originality/value The paper reframes R&D–marketing coordination as capability orchestration rather than functional integration, fusing the Dynamic Capabilities View with Resource Orchestration Theory. The resulting contingency model moves beyond the question of whether integration improves performance toward specifying which configurations improve performance under which conditions, offering both a theoretical architecture and a research agenda organised around generative AI, platform ecosystems and sustainability transitions.

title: The personalization–privacy paradox in social media advertising: a cross-national study of ad attitudes and eWOM
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore how advertising personalization and perceived intrusiveness influence consumers' attitudes toward social media ads and their subsequent electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) behaviors. Using the privacy calculus theory and the theory of planned behavior, we examine whether personalized ads boost positive attitudes and whether intrusiveness diminishes them. Additionally, we analyze how these attitudes translate into positive or negative eWOM, comparing three EU countries (Poland, Portugal and Sweden) that operate under GDPR but differ in digital literacy and privacy concerns. Design/methodology/approach We conducted an online survey of Instagram users in three target countries. After data cleaning, the final samples included N = 337 (Poland), 200 (Portugal) and 196 (Sweden). Respondents rated established multi-item scales for ad personalization, intrusiveness, ad attitude and positive/negative eWOM intent. Data were analyzed using multi-group structural equation modeling to test the hypothesized model and compare effects across countries. Findings The results consistently indicate that higher personalization fosters more positive attitudes toward ads, while greater perceived intrusiveness results in less positive attitudes. Positive ad attitudes, in turn, significantly boost intentions for positive eWOM across all countries. Notably, strong ad attitudes also predict higher intentions for negative eWOM, suggesting ambivalent reactions to personalization. Additionally, perceived intrusiveness diminishes the positive impact of personalization on ad attitudes in Portugal and Sweden (moderation confirmed), but this moderating effect was not significant in Poland. Originality/value This research makes a novel contribution by integrating marketing and information systems frameworks and empirically testing them across diverse national contexts. Integrating privacy calculus theory and the theory of planned behavior frameworks, it addresses both the positive (personalization) and negative (intrusiveness) sides of targeted advertising, a distinction often omitted in single-country studies. To our knowledge, this is among the first cross-country studies to compare these effects within a unified model; by examining Poland, Portugal and Sweden together, the paper offers new insights into how cultural and regulatory contexts shape the personalization–privacy paradox in eWOM outcomes.

title: Technology transfer through inter-firm networks and SMEs’ formal R&D: evidence from Japanese buyer–supplier and ownership linkages
Beyond the classroom: dialogic action for sustainability accounting education and practice
Corporate social responsibility and investors with multiple blockholdings: a monitoring capacity perspective
Consumer vulnerability in artificial intelligence-driven marketing: A paradox theory lens
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming marketing through hyper-personalization, predictive analytics and enhanced customer experience, yet its ethical implications for consumer vulnerability remain undertheorized. We apply a paradox theory lens to identify four tensions in AI-driven marketing: Diversity (included versus excluded), Data (safeguarded versus exploited), Dignity (empowered versus dependent), and Development (informed versus misinformed). We advance a conceptual framework situating these tensions within key boundary conditions (consumer agency, marketer intentionality, and AI opacity) that determine whether AI alleviates or exacerbates consumer vulnerability. In doing so, we extend marketing scholarship on AI-driven marketing, consumer vulnerability, and inclusion by theorizing AI as a relational, dual-sided agent rather than a uniformly empowering or exploitative one, built on a both/and paradox framing. We also translate the framework into strategic guidelines, CARE (Control, Aim, Reveal, and Empathy), that encapsulate our framework’s boundary conditions and dimensions to help practitioners and policymakers act on these tensions in practice.

title: When luxury brands roar: the effect of animal logo types on consumers’ luxury consumption
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how animal logo types of luxury brands influence consumers’ luxury consumption. Design/methodology/approach Based on the Stereotype Content Model, this research investigates whether competent (vs warm) animal logos influence consumers’ luxury consumption through perceived dominance, and how this effect is moderated by message appeal (competitive vs cooperative). The investigation employs a multi-method approach with seven interrelated studies: an exploratory study, an eye-tracking study and five controlled experiments. Findings The results demonstrate that consumers prefer luxury brands featuring competent animal logos over those with warm logos. This preference stems from the ability of competent animal logos to better fulfill consumers’ psychological need for perceived dominance. This effect, however, is appeal-dependent: within cooperative appeals, animal logo type does not significantly influence perceived dominance. Research limitations/implications Moving beyond a focus on animal symbolism, this study centers on visual design expression as the key driver of meaning in animal logos. It examines how such expression shapes consumer perceptions and behavior. This extends the Stereotype Content Model to animal representations in luxury branding and clarifies how consumers decide on luxury purchases. Practical implications This research offers practical implications for luxury goods companies regarding the strategic use of animal logos to drive luxury consumption and enhance brand strategy effectiveness. Originality/value While animal symbolism is widely used in branding, and animal logos are prevalent in luxury contexts, the influence of visual design expression in animal logos on consumer perception and decision-making remains underexplored. This study addresses this significant gap in luxury marketing research.

title: Adaptive management control systems in operations: the reconfiguration of control mechanisms on the shop floor
abstract: Purpose This paper investigates the complexity and dynamics of assembly line managers' management control systems. It examines which mechanisms comprise these systems and how their relevance and configuration change as managers tackle different productivity-related control problems on the shop floor. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts an abductive single case study approach, drawing on interview, observational and archival data from a global automotive supplier. Building on complexity theory and management control research, it analyses line managers' control problems on a U-shaped assembly line. Findings The study identifies three recurrent workforce-related control problems (workforce assignment, managing process interruptions and motivating the team) and shows how five types of management control mechanisms (administrative, cultural, cybernetic, planning and reward) combine into distinct configurations around each control problem. These configurations shift as managers' attention moves between control problems, representing dynamics that can be interpreted through the lens of a complex adaptive system. Practical implications By demonstrating how line managers combine and reconfigure control mechanisms across recurring control problems, this study offers actionable insights for line manager training and for senior managers seeking to support shop floor productivity. Originality/value This study interprets management control systems in operations as complex adaptive systems and introduces the notion of control problem dynamics, showing how shop floor productivity management emerges through the co-evolution of control mechanisms and the control problems they address.
journal_name: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

title: Old and connected versus young and creative: Networks and the diffusion of new scientific ideas
Psychological safety, motivations and change-oriented organizational citizenship behaviour in emergency managers
abstract: Fostering change-oriented organizational citizenship behaviour (CO-OCB) is critical for resilience-building in the public sector, yet the psychological mechanisms driving such behaviour among emergency managers remain underexplored. Drawing on a survey of 869 public employees from emergency management agencies in China, this study examines how psychological safety, creative self-efficacy (CSE), and public service motivation (PSM) influence CO-OCB and tests the moderating role of work autonomy. Results reveal that psychological safety and PSM positively predict CO-OCB, whereas CSE unexpectedly suppresses the effect of psychological safety. Notably, work autonomy moderates the impacts of CSE and PSM on CO-OCB. These findings reveal how psychological safety shapes change-oriented behaviour through distinct but interrelated competence-related and motivational mechanisms within bureaucratic contexts. This study advances public-sector innovation theory by uncovering the nuanced role of psychological safety and by emphasizing the importance of public service motivation in enhancing organizational resilience during institutional reforms and crises.

title: Energy, food and fertilizer price shocks: implications for food security in fragile and conflict affected countries in Sub-Saharan Africa
