Fluid–structure interaction analysis of an asymmetric thin downstream bluff body for a tandem bladeless wind turbine
abstract: The present study investigates a fixed thin downstream bluff body (TDB) as a passive flow-control strategy for enhancing the post-onset oscillatory response and energy-harvesting performance of a bladeless wind turbine operating through flow-induced vibration (FIV). The proposed asymmetric TDB reorganizes the wake interaction between the oscillating primary cylinder and the fixed downstream body, thereby strengthening aerodynamic excitation and fluid–structure energy transfer over the investigated operating range. The experiments examined fifteen TDB geometries grouped according to cross-sectional shape, together with four aspect-ratio values and multiple spacing ratios. The effects of these parameters were evaluated through vibration response, power generation, flow visualization, particle image velocimetry (PIV), proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), pressure recovery, Reynolds shear stress, velocity deficit, turbulent kinetic energy, and enstrophy analyses. The results demonstrate that the introduction of a properly designed TDB fundamentally reorganizes the wake dynamics. An optimum spacing range of 0.3 ≤ Z / D ≤ 0.4 was identified, while AR = 0.17 was the best-performing aspect ratio within the investigated range, resulting in voltage and power enhancements of approximately 56% and 81%, respectively, compared with the baseline configuration without a TDB. Among all investigated geometries, the asymmetric TDB exhibited the best overall performance within the tested configurations, producing approximately 7.5% higher voltage and 15.5% higher power than the primary rectangular TDB, together with a stronger sustained post-onset oscillatory response. Flow-field analyses revealed enhanced wake confinement, increased circulation and vorticity, stronger coherent vortex interaction, delayed pressure recovery, and greater concentration of energy within low-order POD modes. Enstrophy analysis further showed reduced mean enstrophy and transport accompanied by increased fluctuating enstrophy, indicating a transition toward a more coherent and energetically efficient wake. These findings demonstrate that asymmetric downstream bluff-body design provides an effective approach for enhancing fluid–structure energy transfer and improving the viability of bladeless wind energy harvesting technologies.

title: Decarbonizing industrial process heat: energy, economic, and environmental analysis of a high-temperature solar-assisted heat pump using low GWP refrigerants
abstract: Decarbonizing high-temperature industrial processes is essential to achieve global climate neutrality by 2050. This study evaluates the technical, energy, economic, and environmental performance of solar-assisted heat pumps (SAHPs) for industrial laundry applications, including hot water production at 80 °C and pressurized water (steam economizer) at 140 °C. A validated simulation framework was developed to analyze up to 130 combinations of system configurations and refrigerants. Eight configurations were assessed, comparing single-stage (SS) and two-stage cascade (TSC) cycles using ambient air or solar collectors as heat sources. Low-global warming potential (GWP) refrigerants, including hydrofluoroolefins (HFOs) such as R1233zd(E) and R1336mzz(Z), and hydrocarbons such as R600 and R601a, were considered. For hot water production, solar-assisted systems provide more stable performance than air-source configurations, with photovoltaic-thermal heat pumps (PV/T HP, SS) achieving the highest COP values (3–5), depending on refrigerant and climate. For steam generation, only PV/T HP TSC configurations are technically feasible, with COP values of 1.6–2.0. Economic analysis, compared with conventional gas boilers, systems using R1233zd(E) and R600 achieve the highest profitability, with payback periods of 3.5–7 years over a 20-year lifetime. The best configurations reduce CO 2 emissions by up to 50 %. Overall, optimal system design requires balancing energy efficiency and investment costs, with specific refrigerant–cycle combinations outperforming fossil-fuel technologies across different climates.

title: Liquid-Recirculation-Assisted Anion exchange membrane ammonia Electrolysis: Simultaneous Closed-Loop NH3 recovery and improved H2 purity
abstract: Ammonia (NH 3 ) as a hydrogen carrier is limited by the energy-intensive reconversion to high-purity hydrogen at the point of use. Anion exchange membrane (AEM) ammonia electrolysis offers a low-voltage, low-temperature alternative, but unreacted ammonia is emitted at the anode and crosses over to the cathode, degrading both efficiency and hydrogen purity. Here, two alternative recovery units—a pressurized tank and a wet scrubber—were independently integrated with an AEM electrolysis cell. With the pressurized tank, increasing the anode-side pressure from 1 to 10 bar reduced the outlet NH 3 concentration from 3.64 to 0.65 vol% (82.1 %) but increased the cell-electrical specific energy consumption (SEC) from 55.78 to 69.62 k ⁢ W ⁢ h ⁡ / k ⁢ g H 2 (24.8 %). At the matched 240 mA/cm 2 condition, the atmospheric-pressure wet scrubber reduced outlet NH 3 to approximately 0.475 vol% (87.0 %) with an SEC of 55.4 k ⁢ W ⁢ h ⁡ / k ⁢ g H 2 and maintained the outlet concentration at or below 0.50 vol% across the tested current range. The NH 3 -loaded solution was reused once as the anolyte with a 3.7 % increase in SEC at the matched current density, supporting proof-of-concept closed-loop reuse. A pH-dependent emission model indicated that NH 3 re-volatilization is strongly suppressed when the scrubbing-medium pH is around 6. Furthermore, a pressure-sensitivity analysis indicated that operation without a trans -membrane pressure differential avoids an additional pressure-driven NH 3 crossover, while the measured dry-gas composition corresponded to a bulk H 2 purity of 98.1–98.5 %. These results establish the wet scrubber as the simpler and more energy-efficient route for integrating NH 3 emission control, recirculation, and cathodic H 2 -purity improvement in modular or on-site ammonia-to-hydrogen systems.

title: Performance and transient behavior of a hydrogel flat-plate/finned dual-source heat pump under multi-mode heating: An experimental study
abstract: Conventional solar-air dual-source heat pumps employ separate evaporators, complicating system coordination. This paper presents a direct-expansion heat pump with an integrally formed flat-plate/finned dual-source (FFDS) heat exchanger and a thermochromic hydrogel coating—transparent in winter for solar absorption and opaque in summer for solar rejection. Focusing on winter heating, multi-mode experiments (DHW-only, combined intermittent/continuous space heating) were conducted under various weather conditions. Through high-resolution transient measurements, the study innovatively reveals the generation and evolution mechanisms of sawtooth oscillations in temperatures and pressures under real-time EEV dynamic regulation, including phase shift relationships and the attenuation of superheat oscillation amplitude with increasing condensing pressure—a mechanistic explanation rarely addressed in the literature. Comparative experiments quantify the asymmetric sensitivity of evaporator- and condenser-side parameters to environmental disturbances: compared with sunny conditions, overcast conditions reduce evaporating temperature and pressure by 10.42 °C and 0.136 MPa, raise the pressure ratio from 3.71 to 5.13, and lower the average COP from 4.77 to 3.67, while the condenser side varies modestly. Performance evaluation demonstrates the system’s adaptability to different weather scenarios and user demands: even under nighttime continuous heating with no solar energy input, the system maintains stable operation with an average COP of 3.23. These findings deepen the understanding of transient dynamics and multi-mode performance responses of integrated dual-source heat pumps under EEV dynamic regulation, and provide empirical data and insights for the development of stable and reliable control strategies and integrated system designs.

title: Reducing energy consumption in underwater vehicle hovering operations using a variable structure controller
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles and sensor platforms play a crucial role in the long-term monitoring of marine environments; however, their operational endurance is limited by energy constraints. Effective energy management is therefore essential, particularly with regard to actuation mechanisms, which are among the primary consumers of onboard energy. Consequently, control laws that reduce energy consumption while maintaining performance are of significant importance, as they contribute to more efficient energy utilization. The main contribution of this paper is the proposal of a novel depth control law that exploits the passive dynamics of buoyancy-controlled vehicles to save energy during hovering tasks. The proposed control strategy expends energy only in two situations: 1) to counteract conditions in which the system’s natural dynamics is detrimental to control objectives, and 2) to drive the system to rest when it is near the target depth. Both simulation and experimental results show that this approach reduces energy consumption compared to PID-based controllers and to recently reported energy-efficient strategies. Against the latter, the proposed method achieves energy savings of up to 13% while simultaneously reducing the average depth control error by 50%.

title: Design and multi-objective optimization of a novel axially-magnetized rotary-linear permanent magnet generator using grey relational analysis for integrated wind-wave energy conversion systems

Coupled effects of atmospheric stability and terrain slope on wind turbine wake evolution and downstream power performance over hilly terrain
abstract: The rapid deployment of onshore wind farms in complex terrain is an important pathway for expanding wind energy deployment. However, the coupled effects of atmospheric stability and terrain slope on wind turbine wake evolution and downstream power performance remain insufficiently understood, hindering accurate energy-yield assessment and effective wind-farm layout optimization. In this study, high-fidelity large-eddy simulations are conducted to investigate turbine wakes over flat terrain, a gentle hill, and a steep hill under convective, neutral, and stable atmospheric conditions. The results demonstrate that wake evolution and downstream power performance are jointly controlled by atmospheric stability, terrain slope, and upstream turbine wakes. Coriolis-induced wind veer and terrain-induced flow distortion lead to three-dimensional wake deflection, which becomes more pronounced with increasing atmospheric stability and terrain slope. Under stable conditions over the steep hill, the downstream distributions of power loss and power variability exhibit pronounced asymmetry, together with faster power recovery. Momentum-flux analysis shows that this accelerated recovery is primarily driven by downward mean advective transport from the low-level jet rather than by enhanced turbulent mixing. Terrain-induced power loss and variability increase with terrain slope because of intensified flow separation on the leeward side. In contrast, the power loss and variability caused by upstream turbine wakes decrease over steeper terrain because the increased elevation difference reduces direct wake impingement on the downstream rotor. These findings clarify the coupled terrain–stability mechanisms governing wind turbine wakes and provide guidance for energy-yield assessment and turbine layout optimization in complex terrain.

A dynamic and viewing-direction-aware 3D visuospatial analysis framework for indoor environments based on embodied 3D isovist
abstract: Quantitative analysis of dynamic visuospatial experience is increasingly important as behavioural experiments provide fine-grained positional and viewing records. Isovist analysis is a well-established method for visuospatial analysis of architectural spaces, and Embodied 3D Isovist represents one extension of this approach to three-dimensional analysis. However, methods for applying Embodied 3D Isovist to path analysis remain underdeveloped, particularly in representing continuous movement and direction-dependent visual experience. The present study proposes a framework that directly operates on time-series position and viewing direction data. A case study compared grid-like and continuous conditions, limited- and unlimited-FOV conditions, and opposing movement directions along the same path. The results showed that grid-like analysis generally approximated continuous analysis, whereas FOV limitation produced clear direction-dependent differences, particularly in open spaces. The case study also identified a limitation in the original definition of the properties and indicated a potential relationship between dynamic visibility transitions and spatial cognition. The proposed framework extends Embodied 3D Isovist towards analysing dynamic visuospatial experience during movement.

title: Is Australia part of the Pacific? Re-imagining Australia’s Pacific identities and relationships for an ‘Island’ future
abstract: Since the beginning of colonisation, Australian authorities have had a persistent desire to control the Pacific. While Australia is a long-standing key partner for Pacific Island states, there is an underlying discontent with the often domineering and exploitive nature of Australia in the region. Seeking to understand why this approach to diplomacy in the Pacific has been so hard to change for Australia, I suggest it is because ideas of Australia as a powerful regional administrator have become so central to its collective identity that they have been fused into the diplomatic, strategic, and political culture in Canberra. Using lenses of ontological security, narratives, and articulation theory, I examine how this identity has evolved through three vignettes: the initial portrayal of Australia as a Western, continental, colonial controller; the discursive construction of Australian primacy in relation to the Pacific and its peoples; and an examination of recent diplomatic interactions between Australia and Pacific partners. Drawing on Teaiwa’s vision of articulation theory, I suggest these ideas have become akin to a bodily part of Australia’s core identity concerns—and it will generally act to preserve its sense of this self. However, while difficult, change is possible. In a forward-looking coda, I propose that future change is funnelled towards ‘islanding’ Australia. A fundamental reorientation of identity, culture, and practice that embraces Australia’s vulnerability and possibility could open the space for a more productive future with Pacific partners and a more comfortable relationship with Australia’s own core identity.

A platform for change? Core component innovations, complementor adaptation, and multihoming in platform‐based ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Research Summary Digital platforms coordinate complementor innovations through interfaces into their core components. However, when interfaces themselves evolve alongside core component innovations, complementors may exhibit behaviors that are not entirely predictable. Using granular data from Apple's five major iOS releases, we abductively examine App developers’ responses following Apple's core component innovations. We document that, in post‐release periods, complementors simultaneously increase co‐innovation on iOS while being more likely to multihome by diversifying to the competing platform. These choices are further explained by whether architectural changes reflect cross‐platform standardization or platform‐specific differentiation. Standardization spurs both complementor co‐innovation and multihoming, while differentiation reduces diversification tendencies. The patterns that we document reveal an important tension: governing through interfaces enables platforms’ scalability but constrains their ability to control complementors as platforms evolve. Managerial Summary Digital platforms like Apple coordinate large scale innovation through standardized interfaces, but those interfaces must evolve as platforms compete, and the direction of that evolution has consequences managers should attend to. Analyzing Apple's five major iOS releases, we find that architectural changes are associated with increased co‐innovation but also a higher likelihood that developers diversify to a competing platform. This pattern is particularly pronounced when updates bring iOS closer to Android, suggesting that architectural convergence may lower the barriers to cross‐platform expansion for developers. Importantly, this behavior is strongest among highest‐value developers. Platform managers should therefore treat architectural evolution not merely as a technical decision, but as a strategic one with direct implications for ecosystem loyalty, competitive differentiation, and the retention of valuable ecosystem partners.

title: Do Investors Follow Their Heart? The Role of Value Congruence in Guiding Investors' Decisions
abstract: ABSTRACT Retail investors evaluating impact‐oriented opportunities must weigh economic, social, and environmental performance simultaneously, yet it remains unclear why they prioritize these dimensions so differently. We propose that personal values act as a weighting mechanism in multiattribute investment decisions. In a discrete choice experiment with 547 US retail investors, financial performance and risk dominate on average, but altruistic, biospheric, and egoistic values are each associated with greater weight on the corresponding performance dimension; attribute salience also varies across investment domains. Personal values thus help explain preference heterogeneity that demographic characteristics and cognitive biases alone leave unaccounted for.

title: Bank Risk-Taking and Deposits Around Going Concern Opinions
abstract: We investigate bank risk-taking and deposit flows around first-time going concern opinions (GCOs). Although GCOs may strengthen market monitoring, they are also often accused of destabilizing banks by triggering depositor runs. Our evidence is difficult to reconcile with that concern. Uninsured deposits begin to decrease several quarters before the GCO, but insured deposits increase over the same period, leaving total deposits broadly stable around the opinion. This pattern suggests that more sophisticated depositors respond to timelier information than the annual audit report and shift from uninsured to insured funding before the GCO becomes public, whereas insured retail depositors do not exhibit large-scale withdrawals around the GCO. We also document that bank risk measures increase in the quarters leading up to the GCO and then stabilize and subsequently decrease after the opinion. In addition, severe enforcement actions become more likely in the post-GCO period. Taken together, these patterns are consistent with an indirect supervisory channel that may help interpret the post-GCO change in bank risk-taking. Overall, our findings suggest that concerns about GCOs precipitating depositor runs may be overstated and that systematic auditor forbearance is not clearly justified on financial-stability grounds.

title: Institutional Amnesia and the Loss of “The Why Rationale” in Central Government Agencies
abstract: ABSTRACT Data from 115 interviews conducted with officials in the Westminster systems of Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom is used to substantiate a corrosive relationship between institutional amnesia and the ability of public servants to make sense of their organizational context. A process in which public servants question why the policies, procedures, and organizational frameworks that surround them is proposed as one medium through which this relationship operates. Four problematic effects produced by this relationship and process are subsequently analyzed: (1) public servants following but not understanding procedures, (2) inexplicable organizational aspects getting abandoned, (3) the layering of new organizational features on top of old ones, creating complexity, and (4) public service inefficiencies and associated public servant frustration. The article concludes with the implications of this important relationship for public administration scholars and practitioners.

Voltage-Dependent Metabolic Shifts Regulate the Fouling Behavior of the Anaerobic-Anodic Membrane
abstract: Abstract Fouling remains the key barrier to durable membrane operation, against which electrochemical processes offer a promising fouling control strategy. However, the performance of an anodic membrane under anaerobic conditions exhibits significant instability, the mechanism of which remains unclear and represents a critical knowledge gap. This study systematically investigated the response of membrane fouling evolution to gradient electric fields within anodic membranes. A distinct threshold behavior of electric field strength on membrane fouling was observed, with a system-dependent threshold occurring between 0.7 and 1.0 V. Following an initial fouling layer, subthreshold fields (≤0.7 V) exacerbated fouling accumulation, whereas supra-threshold fields (≥1.0 V) slowed down membrane fouling development. Comprehensive analysis revealed that surpassing critical field strength enhanced anodic electron-accepting capacity, likely facilitating microbial extracellular electron release and alleviating reductive pressure. This triggered a nonlinear, threshold-dependent metabolic switch from biosynthesis-dominated to catabolism-enhanced pathways, coupled with quorum quenching that inhibited biofilm maturation. These synergistic transitions underpinned the fouling reversal. This work advances the understanding of anaerobic-anodic membrane fouling from an empirical observation into a threshold-governed electrochemical–microbial switching process, thereby providing the scientific foundation for harnessing this interplay to achieve durable and efficient operation in anaerobic wastewater treatment and resource recovery systems.

title: Evaluating Community-Level Effects of 6PPD-Quinone in a Natural Boreal Lake Ecosystem
abstract: Abstract 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), a transformation product of the tire rubber antioxidant 6PPD, is an emerging contaminant known for its acute toxicity to certain salmonids. However, its potential impacts on aquatic communities remain poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, 6PPD-Q-spiked limnocorrals were deployed in a natural boreal lake, and water chemistry, phytoplankton, zooplankton, and benthic invertebrate communities were assessed over 28 days following a single pulse exposure (0–100 μg/L) simulating stormwater runoff. Waterborne 6PPD-Q concentrations declined by 80–99% by the end of the study, with no detectable effects on water chemistry or aquatic communities. Temporal changes in chlorophyll-a concentrations and zooplankton abundance were attributed to seasonal dynamics rather than 6PPD-Q exposure, and benthic invertebrate community composition remained unchanged. Concurrently, wild-spawned fathead minnow (Pimephales promelas) embryos were exposed to 6PPD-Q-spiked water collected from the limnocorrals. Larval survival declined significantly at 100 μg/L, with altered hatch timing and sublethal effects including reduced growth, changes in eye, yolk sac, and pericardial areas, and altered energy allocation. These effects occurred at 10.6–22.4 μg/L and above, concentrations that exceed those so far reported in surface waters and stormwater by approximately an order of magnitude. Collectively, this study provides the first field-scale assessment of 6PPD-Q effects on aquatic communities and early life-stage fish. Environmental Significance. This study provides the first field-scale assessment of 6PPD-Q impacts on freshwater communities. While broad aquatic communities appeared resilient to short-term exposure scenarios, early life stages of fish responded at concentrations above those currently reported in the environment, identifying developmental end points that warrant attention when assessing the risks of tire-derived contaminants in freshwater ecosystems.

title: Economic Trade and Atmospheric Transport in Shaping China’s Nitrogen Deposition Patterns
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric nitrogen deposition in China is driven not only by local emissions but also by global economic demand and transboundary atmospheric transport. Unraveling these dual influences is critical for effective environmental governance. Here, we integrate an economic-emission analysis with a high-resolution atmospheric chemical transport model to quantify, for the first time, the distinct roles of domestic consumption, international trade, and atmospheric transport in shaping China’s nitrogen deposition patterns. We find that domestic consumption is the dominant contributor, responsible for 67.6% of the total deposition, involving a substantial interprovincial transfer of emissions from affluent coastal provinces to less developed inland regions. International trade attributes 7.8% of China’s deposition to foreign consumption, primarily driven by demand from the USA and Western Europe. In contrast, trans-national atmospheric transport directly accounts for 12.8%, with a disproportionately high impact on ecologically sensitive western China. Natural sources contribute the remaining 11.8%. Our results reveal a complex web of drivers extending beyond China’s borders. Mitigating nitrogen deposition, therefore, requires moving beyond local emission controls to embrace consumption-based accountability and enhanced international cooperation on both trade and atmospheric pollution to protect vulnerable ecosystems.

Exploring hydrogen production from plastic waste for urban transportation in Hong Kong and its environmental impact mitigation: integrating dynamic material flow analysis and life cycle assessment
abstract: Plastic waste to hydrogen technology offers a sustainable clean energy pathway while reducing landfill and incineration burdens. However, its feasibility as a feedstock for urban mobility decarbonization at the city scale remains largely unexplored. Hong Kong, as a densely populated metropolitan region facing substantial plastic waste challenges, presents an ideal case study to assess the viability of plastic-derived hydrogen for transportation applications. This study developed an innovative waste-to-wheel framework to assess the mitigation of environmental impacts on Hong Kong's urban mobility through plastic waste-to-hydrogen technology. Dynamic material flow analysis was used to quantify historical and future plastic waste generation, while life cycle assessment (LCA) was adopted to assess the environmental impacts associated with urban transportation in Hong Kong. The results indicated that accumulated plastic waste in Hong Kong is projected to reach 27.6 million tonnes (Mt) between 2026 and 2050, with polypropylene and polyethylene comprising 58.7% of the total, providing substantial feedstock for hydrogen production. Hydrogen demand in the transportation sector is estimated at 880.1 thousand tonnes of coal equivalent (tce) by 2050 under the hydrogen scenario. LCA results revealed that waste-based hydrogen production achieves the lowest global warming potential at −1.36 kg carbon dioxide equivalent (CO 2 -eq) per kg hydrogen, reducing transportation sector emissions to 193 thousand tonnes CO 2 -eq by 2050, which is 78.2% lower than the business-as-usual scenario. Plastic-derived hydrogen could supply 101.7% (97.5%-105.4%) of cumulative transportation hydrogen demand during 2026-2050. These findings validate plastic waste as a sustainable transportation fuel, guiding Hong Kong's hydrogen and circular economy planning.

title: Soil CH4 and CO2 emissions mediated by water and afforestation in Horqin Sandy Land
abstract: Ecological restoration in arid and semi-arid regions plays a vital role in maintaining regional carbon balance under global change. Although water management and vegetation composition regulate soil carbon cycling, their combined effects on greenhouse gas source/sink dynamics in sandy ecosystems and the underlying microbial mechanisms remain unclear. This study examined sand dunes (Sd) and 35-year-old typical afforestation types including Caragana microphylla Lam. (Cm), Populus simonii Carr. (Ps), Pinus sylvestris var . mongolica Litv. (Pm), and mixed forests of Ps + Pm and Pm + Cm in the Horqin Sandy Land. Through a controlled incubation experiment at 30% and 60% water holding capacity (WHC), we systematically analyzed the effects of afforestation and water management on soil methane (CH 4 ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions. Linear regression analyses of functional gene abundances and environmental factors further revealed microbial mechanisms. All afforested soils acted as CH 4 sinks, Ps, Pm, Ps + Pm, and Pm + Cm showed the strongest CH 4 uptake, correlated with higher pmoA gene abundance and lower mcrA / pmoA . 30% WHC enhanced CH 4 oxidation by improving soil aeration, whereas CO 2 emissions increased significantly under elevated water content. Cm showed the highest CO 2 emissions, whereas mixed forests (Ps + Pm and Pm + Cm) maintained high CH 4 uptake even under high CO 2 emissions. These findings indicate that water management and afforestation legacy interactively shape carbon cycling pathways in sandy ecosystems. Mixed forests optimize microbial community function, balancing carbon cycling efficiency with greenhouse gas mitigation across water regimes, providing a scientific basis for carbon management in ecological restoration of the Horqin Sandy Land and comparable semi-arid regions.

title: River network position and cascade dam effects on macroinvertebrate communities: implications for hierarchical river conservation
abstract: The interplay between the natural gradient of river networks and the fragmentation effects of cascade dams in shaping macroinvertebrate diversity and community assembly remains unclear. This study focused on the middle Jialing River in the upper Yangtze basin, a highly developed area. We quantified taxonomic and functional α- and β-diversity across the river network. Generalized additive models revealed a clear spatial gradient. Dam impacts amplified in distal secondary tributaries and attenuated in proximal mainstem reaches. The strongest dam-related effects occurred in secondary tributaries, where high local damming intensity co-occurred with low background connectivity. Random forests and structural equation modeling showed that dam distance consistently affected diversity. This effect was strong on taxonomic β-diversity in secondary tributaries, with a direct path coefficient of 0.53. Functional β-diversity was highly responsive to dam distance and exhibited a pronounced nestedness pattern in secondary tributaries. Variation partitioning revealed that community assembly mechanisms shifted along the river network. Dispersal limitation dominated at the basin scale. Environmental filtering drove the mainstream and primary tributaries. Secondary tributaries were jointly driven by dam distance, environmental filtering, and spatial constraints. These findings extend the network position hypothesis to regulated rivers by re-parameterizing its dispersal-directionality assumption. We recommend designating secondary tributaries as priority conservation areas, primary tributaries as connectivity management zones, implementing multi-site protection along the mainstream, and incorporating functional β-diversity into routine monitoring as a sensitive indicator for ecological assessment. This study provides new insights into the coupled effects of cascade dams and natural river network structure, offering a scientific basis for hierarchical river management in the upper Yangtze River.

title: Porous geopolymer from cyanobacterial sludge and coal fly ash as shape-stabilizing matrix for thermal energy storage using phase change paraffin
abstract: The consumption of fossil fuels drives both the energy crisis and greenhouse gas emissions, while the accumulation of solid wastes such as coal fly ash (CFA) and cyanobacterial sludge (CS) exerts considerable ecological pressure. This study explores the utilization of CS and CFA as raw materials, employing egg white powder as a surfactant and hydrogen peroxide as a blowing agent to fabricate a highly porous geopolymer (CCG). The organic fibers in CS act as pore templates and reinforcing agents, while their partial degradation in the alkaline environment participates in the gelation process. The optimal formulation comprises a 9 mol/L sodium hydroxide solution, 3 wt% egg white powder, 7 wt% hydrogen peroxide, a CS:CFA mass ratio of 2:8, and a sodium silicate to sodium hydroxide solution ratio of 2.5:1. Following synthesis, CCG underwent vacuum impregnation with phase change paraffin (PCP). The capillary forces within the porous matrix effectively encapsulate the molten PCP, yielding a shape-stabilized phase change composite (CCGP). Relative to CCG the CCGP exhibits a thermal conductivity enhancement of 0.081–0.168 W/(m·K). The solidification and melting enthalpies of the CCGP were 67.58 J/g and 69.23 J/g, respectively, with remarkable thermal stability at temperatures up to 600 °C. This study not only achieves high-value utilization of CS and CFA, but also provides new insights into protein-assisted foaming and fiber pore formation in geopolymer systems, offering guidance for the design of shape-stabilized phase change composites with optimized encapsulation efficiency and long-term thermal stability.

title: Subsidies for innovative technology adoption: Experimental evidence on malaria in Burkina Faso
Does advertising expand the market for hospital services? Evidence from Medicare
abstract: Direct-to-consumer advertising is pervasive in US healthcare markets, but little evidence exists on the effects of advertising by hospitals, second only to drug manufacturers in medical marketing. Advertising may help facilities increase market share by stealing existing patients, expanding the market for hospital care, or both. Regardless, it has important public finance implications due to the large sums of taxpayer funds spent by federal and state governments to subsidize hospital operations and finance care through public insurance programs. This paper provides the first causal evidence on the market expansion effects of hospital advertising. To obtain causal estimates, we leverage the fact that spikes in political advertising significantly crowd out hospital advertising in the same market, motivating an instrumental variables design. Using claims data on the universe of Traditional Medicare beneficiaries, we find that advertising expands aggregate patient volume and spending on inpatient care - though to a modest degree (implied elasticities are 0.06 and 0.05, respectively). Although the overall effect of advertising on hospital outpatient care is small and imprecise, for-profit hospitals obtain higher outpatient Medicare volume and revenue.

The role of immigrant caregivers in improving the welfare of elders and reducing public health costs
abstract: Abstract This paper examines the impact of paid migrant home care on elderly health outcomes in Italy. The results show that an increase in migrants’ presence reduces both the frequency and duration of hospitalisations. Specifically, a 1 percentage-point increase in the migrant-to-elderly ratio leads to a decline in long-term and rehabilitation inpatient (LRI) admissions of 118 cases per 100,000 elders, with no measurable effect on acute inpatient stays. There is also a reduction in the average length of stay of 0.141 days, rising to 0.956 days for LRI cases. These effects are driven by diagnoses related to traumatic injuries, musculoskeletal, and genitourinary conditions — areas closely linked to home mobility and care management. Back-of-the-envelope calculations suggest that the average annual increase of 1.3 percentage points in the migrant-to-elderly ratio observed during the study period corresponds to an 8% reduction in elderly LRI hospitalisation costs, equivalent to 252.3 million euros.

title: Carbon taxes crowd out low-carbon choices: Evidence from a consumer experiment
abstract: We examine the impact of a carbon tax on consumer choices via a large-scale online randomized controlled trial. Higher taxes generally reduce the demand for high-carbon goods. Compared to an import tax, a carbon tax reduces demand when the tax is zero (i.e., announced but not levied) but leads to relatively higher demand for high-carbon goods when a positive tax is introduced. This difference in demand responses, despite identical prices, is concentrated among climate-concerned consumers. Our findings suggest that carbon taxes can crowd out the effect of climate concerns on consumer choices, with important implications for policy.

title: The trade-off between minimal instability and larger improvements over deferred acceptance
abstract: The celebrated Efficiency-Adjusted Deferred Acceptance mechanism (EADA) improves the efficiency of the DA algorithm via consented priority violations. Notwithstanding its many merits, we show that EADA can improve only two students when an alternative mechanism that Pareto-dominates DA could benefit all but one student. This shortfall in the number of students improved is not exclusive of EADA but extends to all setwise minimally unstable mechanisms, i.e. those that generate a set of blocking pairs that is never a strict superset of that of another mechanism. The incompatibility between number of students improved and minimal instability disappears when blocking pairs are compared cardinally rather than by set inclusion. In some problems, EADA can be doubly dominated: improving fewer students while generating more blocking pairs.
