Impact of slurry additives on nitrogen emissions, grass agronomy and soil microbial communities following slurry landspreading
abstract: This study assessed the effects of specific slurry additives on nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions, grass herbage yield and N uptake and soil microbial communities. The experimental work was conducted on two soil types: i) a moderately to poorly drained fine loam and ii) an imperfectly drained clay loam over two growing seasons. Cattle slurry was applied in three split applications at both sites simulating trailing shoe application method and the treatments were control (no treatment), unamended slurry, slurry + sulphuric acid, slurry + biochar, slurry + gypsum and urea + urease inhibitor N-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide (NBPT) (NBPT-urea). Nitrous oxide was measured during the growing period using the static chambers and dry matter yield was measured at every harvest. Ammonia (NH 3 ) was also quantified at one of the sites, therefore NH 3 responses are site-specific. Ammonia was measured within the first week of slurry application using dynamic chambers coupled with a photoacoustic gas analyser. Soil samples were collected after the end of the experiment for microbial analysis at both sites. The acidified slurry increased grass yield by more than one tonne ha −1 , increased plant N recovery by 21 to 24 kg N ha −1 , suggesting improved nitrogen conservation may have contributed to these agronomic benefits, and increased fungal abundance however, it also increased N 2 O on one occasion. The other slurry amendments did not have significant effect on N 2 O. The cumulative N 2 O emissions from the moderately drained soil were significantly lower than the imperfectly drained soil. None of the amendments significantly reduced NH 3 emissions in the moderately to poorly drained soil, while biochar increased NH 3 during a single application timing.

title: Unlocking the carbon reduction potential of building integrated photovoltaics beyond rooftops in an urban core considering inter building shading
Sustainable production of ultrahigh-temperature thermal energy storage particles from molten steel slag
abstract: Steel slag (SS), a high-volume byproduct (150 kg/ton steel) with severe disposal burdens, poses critical environmental challenges. To transform this waste into value, we propose the novel TERSEG protocol–a sustainable valorization route that, for the first time, simultaneously enables ultrahigh-temperature thermal energy storage (TES) particle production from molten SS via centrifugal granulation and recovers its >1400 °C waste heat. By modifying molten SS with blast furnace slag (BFS) to drastically reduce its viscosity by ∼90% (to 0.23 Pa s at 1500 °C), we overcome prior barriers to granulation. The engineered particles (1-3 mm) exhibit exceptional thermal stability (<1% mass loss over 10 cycles at 400-1000 °C), good sphericity (axis ratio of 1.5), and low porosity (<4%), making them ideal TES materials. This approach recovers >1400 °C waste heat and converts hazardous slag into functional materials. The TES particle production scalability is demonstrated via an empirical correlation validated across broad operational conditions. This approach pioneers a sustainable valorization route that simultaneously recovers >1400 °C waste heat and converts hazardous slag into functional TES materials. This work provides a circular economy strategy for the steel industry, diverting slag from landfills, reducing industrial CO2 footprint, and advancing net-zero goals.

title: Ranking green finance instruments and finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms within the environmental, social, and governance (ESG) framework: Empirical evidence from Saudi Arabia's petrochemical industry
abstract: The petrochemical industry faces increasing pressure to decarbonize due to its high energy intensity, carbon emissions, and environmental footprint. This study evaluates and ranks green finance instruments and finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms within the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework to identify the highest-ranked mechanisms for supporting the sustainable transition of Saudi Arabia's petrochemical industry. A two-stage multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework integrating the Analytic Network Process (ANP) and fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) was employed to assess six alternatives comprising four green finance instruments and two finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms against three ESG dimensions and fifteen industry-specific sub-criteria. The results show that the Environmental dimension carries the highest priority, followed by Governance and Social, highlighting the importance of measurable environmental outcomes supported by robust governance structures. Among the evaluated alternatives, green tax policies ranked first, followed by green credit mechanisms and investor risk mitigation instruments. The findings suggest that progressive environmental taxation, preferential green lending, and blended-finance mechanisms are better positioned to support industrial decarbonization while limiting abrupt cost pressures during the transition. Furthermore, the effectiveness of green bonds and emission trading systems depends on transparent governance, regulatory compliance, and credible sustainability reporting frameworks. This study provides policy insights for aligning industrial finance with Saudi Vision 2030, the Saudi Green Initiative, and the Kingdom's 2060 net-zero target, while offering a practical decision-support framework for prioritizing sustainable finance in energy-intensive industries.

title: Reconfiguring urban mining: Orchestrating multi-actor E-waste supply chains for circular value recovery through an integrated DEMATEL–BWM–Agent-Based Modeling framework
abstract: The accelerating generation of e-waste in developing economies presents both an environmental challenge and an opportunity for circular value recovery through urban mining, yet fragmented coordination among heterogeneous formal and informal actors limits the realization of this potential. This study addresses the gap between causal diagnosis and dynamic simulation by proposing an integrated DEMATEL–BWM–Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) framework for reconfiguring multi-actor e-waste supply chains toward enhanced circular value recovery. The framework was operationalized through ten expert panelists who validated fifteen coordination factors. DEMATEL identified causal structures and systemic influence, BWM established strategic priorities, and ABM translated these findings into agent-level behavioral rules and environmental conditions across six orchestration scenarios. The DEMATEL analysis revealed regulatory and institutional factors as primary causal drivers, with regulatory enforcement exerting the strongest systemic influence. The BWM analysis confirmed regulatory enforcement as the most strategically important factor. The ABM simulation demonstrated that combined orchestration achieved a 134.81% improvement in recovered material and a 100% collection rate, while economic incentives provided the best overall multi-metric performance. The constant recovery rate across all scenarios confirmed that improvements were driven by increased formal participation and collection throughput rather than technological efficiency, underscoring systemic coordination failures as the primary barrier to circular value recovery. The priority-causal matrix identified regulatory factors and formal-informal integration as priority intervention points offering both high causal influence and strategic importance. These findings are conditional on expert-elicited parameters and should be interpreted as exploratory simulation evidence rather than externally validated prediction. This study provides a methodological foundation for bridging causal diagnosis, strategic prioritization, and dynamic simulation in circular supply chain research, offering practical guidance for policymakers and practitioners seeking to unlock the value of the urban mine in developing economy contexts.

title: From past trends to future costs: The influence of economic parameter selection on building life cycle costs in Belgium
Solvothermal carbonization of waste activated sludge using deep eutectic solvents: A solvent-directed route to tunable biochar properties
abstract: The disposal of waste activated sludge (WAS) poses a persistent environmental challenge. While hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) enables sludge valorization without pre-drying, the resulting hydrochar often exhibits low carbon content, high nitrogen levels and inferior fuel properties. This study aimed to determine whether the acidity/basicity and composition of preformed DES-based media could redirect the carbonization pathways of WAS compared with conventional aqueous HTC. Unlike previous DES-assisted HTC systems, in which low-dose DESs are added to water-dominated media, the preformed DES-based media replaced the conventional bulk aqueous medium. Acidic DES showed characteristics consistent with enhanced dehydration, decarboxylation, and condensation characteristics, producing a biochar with substantially higher carbon content (21.97% vs . 9.60% for HTC), low H/C (1.57) and O/C (0.41) atomic ratios, relatively enhanced aromatic character, reduced hydrophilicity, and higher thermal stability (dominant combustion peak at 445.1 °C). In contrast, alkaline DES was associated with enhanced hydrolysis and solubilization, yielding a carbon-depleted, highly hydrophilic residue. Neutral DES exhibits intermediate behavior, producing an oxygen-enriched surface. Overall, DES chemistry produced distinct transformation pathways and tunable biochar properties relative to conventional HTC, providing insights into solvent-mediated regulation of sludge-derived carbon materials.

title: The gap between law and practice: CSR decoupling in Tanzania's mining sector post-regulatory mandate
abstract: This study contributes to CSR decoupling theory by examining stakeholder perceptions of Tanzania's 2017 mandatory Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) regulation through a case study of two major gold mines in the Geita and Mara regions. Using a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design in which we first collected survey data and then explained them through qualitative interviews, we find that respondents report CSR initiatives have become more standardised following the regulation, with more projects in education, health, and water infrastructure. However, the research reveals substantial challenges, including patterns consistent with CSR decoupling, where compliance is often symbolic rather than substantive. Bureaucratic delays, limited community involvement, and sustainability issues further undermine the regulation's effectiveness. Analysed through Institutional and Stakeholder Theories, the findings indicate that while formal practices have changed following regulatory pressure, the regulation is not perceived to have fostered genuine community ownership. The study recommends policy reforms to enforce participatory planning, independent auditing, and post-implementation support to bridge the gap between regulatory intent and community benefit.

title: Construction and energy-consumption analysis of a carbon capture heating system based on waste heat utilization in a coal-fired power plant
abstract: Conventionally, the heat of the reboiler in monoethanolamine (MEA)-based post-combustion CO 2 capture (PCC) system is supplied by intermediate-pressure extraction steam which temperature is higher than the needed, causing energy losses and capture cost increases. This study develops a staged, synergistic heat-supply scheme for a 600 MW unit, featuring exhaust-steam dominance, flue-gas-heat compensation and minimal extraction steam as backup. Low-pressure exhaust-steam heat is upgraded by a compression heat pump and converted to reboiler via flashing, while the waste heat of tail-end flue-gas is recovered through a closed-cycle water loop and delivered to the reboiler via water-water heat exchange and flashing; the extraction steam is introduced only to minimally close the heat balance when waste heat is insufficient. A coupled unit-PCC model is established in Ebsilon and Aspen Plus, and steady-state simulations are performed at 100%/75%/60%/50%/40% THA, followed by improved grey wolf optimizer (IGWO) optimization with the levelized cost of CO 2 capture (LCOC) as the objective. At 0.01 MPa back pressure, the proposed waste-heat strategy reduces LCOC by 19.96%, 13.57%, 11.59%, 9.64% and 6.63% across the five THA conditions relative to the benchmark, while increasing the overall energy utilization rate by 11.4% on average. At 100% THA, the waste heat utilization rate remains 92%-94% and the specific capture energy decreases from 3.20 to 3.06 GJ·tCO 2 −1 . The results demonstrate that the proposed staged framework enables effective substitution of high-grade extraction steam by in-plant low-grade waste heat over a wide load range, providing a practical pathway for cost-effective decarbonization retrofits of coal-fired units.

title: Microbial community shifts accompany divergent soil carbon recovery after aquaculture-pond restoration across China's coastal wetlands
abstract: Aquaculture-pond restoration may rebuild coastal soil carbon, but gains in soil organic carbon (SOC) do not necessarily indicate lower lability or uniform microbial responses. We compared aquaculture ponds and adjacent restored wetlands at 10 sites across temperate, subtropical, and tropical China. SOC, microbial biomass carbon (MBC), dissolved organic carbon (DOC), and easily oxidizable carbon (EOC) were measured at 0–15 and 15–30 cm in 160 samples, and carbon pool management index (CPMI) components were calculated. Surface-soil bacterial communities and FAPROTAX-inferred functions were characterized at three sites. Restoration increased SOC at most sites and surface MBC at five, but carbon-pool responses differed among regions. Operationally non-labile carbon (C SS = SOC − EOC), an operational estimate of less-labile carbon rather than a directly measured persistent carbon pool, increased at Yancheng, Minjiang River Estuary, Zhanjiang, and Dongzhai Port. Caofeidian, Hangzhou Bay, Zhangjiang River Estuary, and Beilun River Estuary had high carbon pool activity indices, producing CPMI values of 239.78–363.74% and indicating labile-carbon enrichment rather than uniform stabilization. Bacterial community structure was dominated by geographic separation: pond and restored samples remained close within sites, whereas alpha diversity decreased at Caofeidian, changed little at Minjiang River Estuary, and increased at Dongzhai Port. Restoration also altered dominant genera and inferred functions, including greater representation of plant-polymer degradation functions in some restored soils. DOC accounted for 46.25% of the fitted variation in the 10 dominant genera and was positively associated with Sulfurimonas , SOC, and C SS . Pond-to-wetland restoration therefore followed multiple carbon-recovery trajectories, ranging from labile-carbon pulses to accumulation of a less labile fraction. Assessments should integrate SOC quantity, carbon lability, and microbial associations.

title: Cold-season grazing better sustains ecosystem multifunctionality than warm-season grazing in Tibetan alpine steppe
abstract: Grazing season profoundly shapes vegetation and soil properties in alpine grasslands, yet its effects on ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF) remain poorly understood. Here, we compared grazing exclusion (GE), moderate-intensity warm-season grazing (WG), and herder-managed cold-season grazing (CG) in a cold-season pasture of the alpine steppe on the Tibetan Plateau to evaluate how seasonal grazing influences species diversity, community biomass, soil physicochemical properties, and EMF. Relative to GE, WG reduced grass dominance but increased sedge and forb proportion, while also decreasing plant height and aboveground biomass (AGB), and lowered EMF. By contrast, CG was associated with higher plant diversity and significantly elevated soil total carbon (TC) while maintaining AGB at levels comparable to GE. Effect-size analysis showed that WG significantly reduced EMF relative to GE whereas the reduction under CG did not reach significance. Correlation and path analyses further indicated that, under WG, multifunctionality was chiefly associated with the biomass pathway, which was positive but insufficient to counterbalance the direct negative effect of grazing, whereas no significant plant diversity or soil nutrient pathway was detected. Under CG, EMF was jointly associated with plant biomass, plant diversity and soil nutrients. These findings highlight the critical role of grazing season in maintaining ecosystem multifunctionality in alpine steppe, suggesting that, in cold-season pastures of the central Tibetan Plateau, cold-season grazing represents a more sustainable strategy than warm-season grazing for balancing forage production and ecological conservation.

title: Function-based and PCA-derived soil health assessments reveal convergent land-use responses and functional trade-offs in Brazilian drylands
abstract: Drylands are highly vulnerable to soil degradation, yet soil-health assessments remain limited for agroecosystems in the Brazilian semi-arid region, and the consistency between diagnoses produced by different assessment frameworks remains poorly understood. This study compared two soil-health assessment methods and evaluated land-use effects on soil health across Brazilian dryland agroecosystems. Soil health was assessed using (i) a soil-function framework integrating chemical, physical, and biological indicators into five functional domains and a multifunctionality metric and (ii) a variance-weighted soil health index (SHI) derived from principal component analysis (PCA). Measurements were obtained from the 0-30 cm layer across three semi-arid sites of Brazil (Sobral-CE, Betânia do Piauí-PI, and Petrolina-PE). Across sites, several diversified agroecosystems showed soil-health scores comparable to native vegetation at the time of sampling and, in some cases, higher scores for specific soil functions. The two frameworks captured similar land-use patterns but differed in indicator contributions: the PCA-derived SHI emphasized chemical variation, whereas the soil-function framework highlighted function-specific strengths and limitations. Soil health interaction functional trends showed that management effects were often expressed as functional trade-offs rather than uniform gains across all functions. Together, the results indicate that the two frameworks provide convergent overall diagnoses but complementary information, with the function-based assessment offering additional resolution for interpreting functional strengths, limitations, and trade-offs. These findings provide a consistent basis for improving soil-health assessment strategies and supporting sustainable land-use management across environmentally vulnerable dryland agroecosystems.

title: Variance-based global sensitivity analysis of a stochastic Collision Risk Model: how wind turbine parameters impact seabirds
abstract: To achieve the United Nation's goal of net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, we must create a world powered by renewable energy. This will rely on large-scale infrastructure projects, which must be developed with consideration for the natural environment. Offshore wind farms (OWFs), in particular, must balance the collision risk that turbines pose to seabirds with green energy targets. Within the UK and most of Europe, collision risk modelling (CRM) is a required component of Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs) and integral for developers and regulators to gauge the risk an OWF development poses to seabird populations. Despite this, how different combinations of OWF parameters may impact collision risk estimates is poorly quantified. We assess the sensitivity of the stochastic CRM to seven key OWF parameters. Using variance-based global sensitivity analysis methodologies, we quantify results for six seabird species deemed at high risk of turbine collision. We find that the estimate of annual bird-turbine collisions is most sensitive to variation in the number of turbines and the distance between blade tip height and highest astronomical tide (air gap), whereby increasing turbine number and decreasing air gap contributed to increased collision rates. A smaller number of large turbines with greater energy output (larger rotor radius) reduced collision risk per unit energy output. These results quantify the impact of OWF parameter variation on seabird collision risk, which could be used to inform design envelopes, focusing the number of turbine scenarios that developers consider within EIAs and maximising cost-effectiveness whilst minimising seabird collision risk.

title: Expansion toward risk: China's urban growth reshapes population exposure to compound environmental pressures
abstract: Rapid urban expansion is altering the distribution of environmental benefits and risks. As cities grow outward, newly developed areas may face elevated exposure to multiple environmental pressures, raising concerns about whether urbanization is inadvertently exposing population toward more adverse environmental conditions. To investigate this, we use population-weighted exposure model to quantify three key environmental exposures in China's newly built-up areas from 2000 to 2018: blue-green space exposure (BGE), PM 2.5 exposure (PME), and heat stress exposure (HSE). By integrating SOM–K-means clustering and Bayesian Networks, we identify the evolution of typical environmental exposure combinations and examine their conditional dependencies. Results show that, from 2010 to 2018, BGE slightly improves, PME shows greater balance but persistent risks, while HSE intensified significantly. Clustering analysis identifies three distinct environmental exposure types: Ecological Deficiency (ED), High Environmental Cost (HEC), and Eco-Advantaged under Heat (EAH). In 2010, ED is the most prevalent type (1133 counties; 55.5%), followed by HEC (792 counties; 38.8%) and EAH (115 counties; 5.6%). By 2018, EAH increases to 386 counties (18.4%), while ED and HEC decline to 1052 (50.1%) and 664 (31.6%) counties, respectively. Notably, 466 ED counties transition to HEC, making ED-to-HEC the largest single transition. 146 counties transition from ED to EAH, indicating ecological improvement accompanied by greater heat stress. Together, these changes reveal a pattern of urban expansion toward risks. Bayesian Networks further reveal a reconfiguration in the conditional dependency structure of environmental exposures, moving from a relatively constrained dependency pattern toward a more interconnected configuration, with BGE becoming more centrally embedded in the network. This study contributes a novel integrative framework for understanding how urban expansion reshapes population exposure to compound environmental pressures and provides insights to inform risk-aware and equitable urban governance.

title: SHAP-based interpretable sparse autoencoder-neural network framework for electric vehicle energy consumption forecasting
abstract: Accurate energy consumption (EC) prediction for different road conditions is critical for battery management, regenerative braking control, and range estimation in battery electric vehicles (BEVs). However, conventional models trained on raw telemetry data often fail to capture complex driving dynamics due to noise and redundancy in high-dimensional inputs. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel hybrid interpretable framework that combines the sparse autoencoder, neural networks, and SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) (SAE-NN-SHAP), which effectively enables denoising, features extraction, reduces dimensionality, captures complex nonlinear characteristics and interpretable EC estimation, utilizing a real-world BEV dataset from a downloadable dynamometer database. Firstly, the enhanced SAE compresses the input space into 25 compact yet essential and meaningful information-dense latent features. Secondly, this representation is then fed into a Bayesian-optimized NN regressor. Both instantaneous (kW) and trip-level (Wh/km) EV-EC were estimated using the meaningful latent features. Thirdly, the proposed SAE-NN achieves the highest R 2 (0.991) and lowest root mean squared error (RMSE) (1.270) and mean absolute error (MAE) (0.930) among all evaluated models, reducing error by 96.67% relative to a conventional NN trained on raw features and by 14.19% relative to the strongest baseline; at the trip level, predicted and actual EC differ by less than 1% across unseen trips’ driving conditions. Finally, the innovative end-to-end SHAP-based interpretability method, combined with SAE-NN encoder weights and latent feature mapping, identifies the specific driving-dynamics factors influencing EC, including speed, regeneration, braking, torque, battery dynamics, etc. The findings provide physically meaningful explanations and actionable insights for an accurate EC and range estimation, proactive and intelligent energy management approach.

title: How can new energy vehicle adoption affect urban ecological resilience? Evidence from a double/debiased machine learning method
abstract: New energy vehicles (NEVs) are increasingly regarded as a driver of energy transition. However, few scholars have conducted quantitative research on the impact of the large-scale adoption of NEVs on urban ecological resilience (UER). Based on the Pressure-State-Response framework adopted to assess UER, this study utilizes panel data from 294 cities in China from 2017 to 2023 and applies a double/debiased machine learning approach to analyze the impact of NEV adoption on UER and the mechanisms driving this effect. The findings yield four main conclusions. First, the adoption of NEVs significantly increases UER. A 1% rise in NEV stock leads to a 0.0132% increase in UER, and this outcome remains stable through multiple robustness tests. Second, the mechanism exploration demonstrates that the adoption of NEVs improves UER through three channels: industrial structure upgrading, boosting green technological innovation capabilities, and raising public environmental awareness. Third, heterogeneity analysis reveals that NEV adoption has a stronger effect on UER in western cities, non-resource-based cities, and cities with stricter environmental regulations. Fourth, sub-dimensional analysis indicates that the adoption of NEVs mainly improves the state criterion and response criterion of UER, while improvements in the pressure criterion occur only in non-resource-based cities and cities with stricter environmental regulations. This study offers empirical evidence demonstrating how NEV adoption contributes to UER and drives sustainable development, emphasizing that this process requires participation from multiple stakeholders including governments, enterprises, and the public.

title: Land‐Use Thresholds and Spatial Regulation Oriented Toward Ecosystem Service Supply–Demand Balance: A Case Study of Jiangxi Province
abstract: ABSTRACT Imbalances between ecosystem service (ES) supply and demand constrain ecological governance and sustainable development. While spatial patterns of these imbalances have been widely studied, less attention has been paid to the land‐use thresholds and regulatory mechanisms needed to maintain ES balance. Using Jiangxi Province as a case study, we developed a threshold‐based spatial regulation framework integrating ESs supply–demand ratio (SDR) analysis, key land‐use type identification, and management zoning. We quantified the spatiotemporal supply and demand of four ESs—carbon sequestration (CS), habitat quality (HQ), water yield (WY), and soil conservation (SC)—from 2003 to 2023. By combining boosted regression tree and segmented regression, we identified key land‐use types affecting ESs balance and their proportional thresholds, and used segmented regression breakpoints for differentiated spatial zoning. The results showed that although the supply of ESs generally exceeded demand, the imbalance intensified over time, particularly for WY and HQ, accompanied by significant spatial heterogeneity. Built‐up land, cropland, and forest land are the dominant land use types affecting the balance of ESs. Built‐up land negatively affected CS and HQ, cropland positively affected WY, HQ, and SC, forest land supported CS and WY, and water area promoted SC. Although land use in Jiangxi remained within the overall balance threshold, some areas approached critical points, with WY showing the smallest balanced area (75.39%). Based on current land‐use structure and ESs thresholds, three ESs management zones and 27 integrated zones were delineated, and differentiated land‐use regulation strategies were proposed, providing a scientific basis for ESs‐oriented spatial governance.

title: Carbon emission and health impacts of remote working: A case study of the Helsinki capital region
abstract: Remote working can reduce commuting-related carbon emissions but may also lower population physical activity levels. This study examines these trade-offs in the Helsinki Capital Region by modelling changes in commuting and worktime travel under three scenarios: no remote work, current levels, and full potential uptake. We combine demographic data, the Finnish National Travel Survey, public transport schedules, and official transport demand models to estimate impacts on CO 2 emissions and active travel. Commuting volumes are taken from demographic data containing home and workplace information of workers, and worktime trips are modelled using an agent-based synthetic population model. Under the full remote work scenario, commuting-related emissions decrease by approximately 72.9 tonnes per day, a 16.7% reduction compared to current levels. However, rebound trips during working hours offset 71.3% of these potential savings, even after accounting for reduced workplace-based trips. Health impacts were assessed using the WHO Health Economic Assessment Tool. Compared to a baseline with no remote work, current remote working levels are associated with approximately 42 additional premature deaths annually due to reduced physical activity, with a further 31 deaths under full remote work conditions. Conversely, if commuting time were repurposed for walking or cycling, up to 71 premature deaths could be avoided under current conditions and 137 under full remote working. The findings highlight the interrelationship between environmental and health dimensions of remote work. While remote working involves clear trade-offs, integrated policy approaches that combine emission reduction strategies and promotion of physical activity while limiting rebound travel are needed to achieve substantial co-benefits.
journal_name: Environment and Planning B Urban Analytics and City Science

title: Contested spatialities of renewable energy expansion—Introduction to the theme issue
abstract: Renewable energy increasingly complements fossil fuels in meeting rising global energy demand. Yet its rollout is neither even nor free of conflict. This theme issue foregrounds the spatialities and scales of renewable energy infrastructures and examines the deeply contested nature of energy transition efforts. Drawing on case studies from Morocco, Jordan, Namibia, Mexico, Brazil, Peru and Ecuador, the contributions offer insights into recent regional developments and highlight transregional and cross-scalar interrelations. They connect place-based research on contested energy projects in political ecology, geography and anthropology with nation-focused analyses of energy transition policy, and approach scale as an unfolding field of contestation. In doing so, they challenge notions of a homogeneous “local” in analyses of energy conflict and move beyond methodological nationalism while still recognizing the significance of the national scale. Together, the theme issue demonstrates the value of relational approaches for disentangling and understanding the contested geographies of contemporary renewable energy expansion.

title: The AI debate is missing half the system
abstract: Last month, leading executives of artificial intelligence (AI) companies warned the United Nations Security Council about the risks of losing human control over this rapidly advancing technology. Their recommendations focused heavily on safeguards, evaluation, and governance of AI models and systems, largely overlooking the risks that arise from the interactions of AI with people and institutions. AI safety needs to be addressed at the level of the human–AI system, not the AI model alone.

Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
abstract: The underlying mechanism of the thermal Hall effect generated by phonons in a variety of insulators is yet to be identified. In this work, we report on a sizable thermal Hall conductivity in nickel phosphorus trisulfide (NiPS 3 ), a van der Waals stack of honeycomb layers with a zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The longitudinal (κ aa ) and the transverse (κ ab ) thermal conductivities peak at the same temperature, and the thermal Hall angle, at this peak, respects a previously identified bound. The amplitude of κ ab is extremely sensitive to the amplitude of magnetization along the b axis but is not correlated with the phonon mean free path, which points to an intrinsic origin.

title: Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity
abstract: Lifestyle-related type 2 diabetes and associated obesity (diabesity) affect >2.5 billion people worldwide and impose nearly $3 trillion in annual health care costs. We developed an implantable, wirelessly powered electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization (ECHO) device containing platinum-decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in graphite felt that enabled selective, electrically tunable oxidation of blood glucose to renally cleared gluconate. In type 2 diabetic mice, wireless, low-power activation (0.75 volts, 10 milliamperes) restored glucose homeostasis within 1 hour, shifted metabolism from glucose to lipid utilization, reduced body weight and triglycerides, and increased circulating free fatty acids and ketone bodies without detectable hypoglycemia or adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects during 6 weeks of treatment. Coupling this ECHO device to a commercial continuous glucose monitoring system enabled autonomous, smartphone-controlled, drug-free closed-loop management of experimental diabesity.

title: Visualizing symmetry-broken Chern insulators and their quantum melting
abstract: In the presence of a magnetic field, electronic states of moiré quantum materials develop a Hofstadter spectrum that provides a distinctive setting for studying the interplay between band topology and strong electron-electron interaction. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we studied Hofstadter’s states in bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride and directly visualized the formation of interaction-driven symmetry breaking Chern insulators. Our measurements revealed the formation of phases that double, triple, or quadruple the moiré unit cell at fractional filling of the Hofstadter bands as well as states with complex intra–unit cell wave functions. We visualized two distinct quantum phenomena in different Chern states, including quantum melting driven by the appearance and proliferation of topological defects and a quantum transition co-occurring with phase competition and separation.

title: BAK and BAX form a multiprotein complex to drive mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death
abstract: The apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK, once activated, form homo-oligomers to trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), activating the apoptosome and caspases. Activation of BAX-BAK without apoptosome activation triggers sustained efflux of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and caspase-independent cell death. However, the molecular basis of mtDNA efflux remains unclear. We purified a macromolecular complex comprising BAK, BAX, activator BH3-only molecules, voltage-dependent anion channels 1 and 2 (VDAC1 and VDAC2), and prohibitins that released mtDNA from mitoplasts. BAX-BAK activation resulted in VDAC closure, mitochondrial calcium influx, and mtDNA efflux. Loss of VDAC1, VDAC2, or prohibitins prevented BAX-BAK activation–induced mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death without affecting MOMP or mitochondrial inner membrane herniation. These findings support differential regulation of cytochrome c and mtDNA efflux by distinct BAX-BAK complexes.

title: Intron retention regulates STAT2 function and associates with immunotherapy response in lung cancer
abstract: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti–programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet
abstract: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.

title: Decoupled self-assembled monolayer and perovskite deposition for efficient flexible solar modules
abstract: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of flexible perovskite solar modules (PSMs) are less than those of their rigid devices because surface hydroxyls desorption on flexible substrates, which disrupts self-assembled monolayer (SAM) anchoring and perovskite crystallization. We developed a decoupled SAM-perovskite codeposition strategy that accelerates SAM anchoring by reducing the SAM-perovskite interaction and ameliorates perovskite crystallization. The certified PCE with phenethylammonium iodide as the passivation molecule was 20.2% on PSMs with device areas of 750 cm 2 . With 1,3-diaminopropane dihydroiodide as the passivator, the PCE of 22.0% for a device area of 14.55 cm 2 decreased by 8% after 1044 hours under maximum power point tracking at 85°C and 65% relative humidity. The devices pass all sequences of an international commercialization assessment standard for flexible portable PSMs.

title: Electronic bound states in the continuum in a two-dimensional metal
abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are quantum states that remain localized despite lying within a continuum of extended, delocalized states. Whereas optical BICs have been realized in photonic systems, achieving electronic bound states embedded in a metallic background remains an ongoing challenge. In this study, we used scanning tunneling microscopy to identify two defect-induced electronic states that remain localized within the metallic continuum of Pd 5 AlI 2 , a two-dimensional van der Waals metal. Our calculations suggest that electron-hopping interference on the decorated checkerboard lattice of Pd 5 AlI 2 gives rise to a (quasi) flat band built from spatially localized eigenstates that are orthogonal to the dispersive continuum. Atomic defects within this frustrated lattice shift the associated flat-band localized states into the metallic continuum, forming robust, symmetry-protected BICs.

title: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

Natural product biosynthesis by guanidine prenyltransferases in plants and bacteria
abstract: Guanidine exists almost exclusively as a resonance-stabilized cation, making its direct enzymatic functionalization challenging. We identified the cyanobacterial enzyme NosH, which catalyzes direct prenyl transfer to free guanidine. Structural and mechanistic analyses revealed guanidine activation by a two-aspartate clamp coupled to prenyl-donor binding through a distinct catalytic architecture. Guided by these features, we identified a large family of guanidine prenyltransferases across bacteria and plants. Plant enzymes produced guanidine alkaloids such as galegine in vitro and heterologous expression of a plant ortholog in Nicotiana benthamiana produced galegine in planta, providing a direct enzymatic link to plant-specialized metabolism.

title: Imaging electron-hole asymmetry in the quantum melting of generalized Wigner crystals
abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials provide a versatile platform to explore phase transitions in strongly correlated systems. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we imaged the density-driven melting of generalized Wigner crystals (GWCs) and Mott insulators (MIs) in electron-doped, near-60°–twisted molybdenum diselenide bilayers featuring a triangular moiré superlattice. We observed notable electron-hole asymmetry in GWC melting: Hole-doped GWCs yielded interaction-driven disordered states, whereas electron-doped GWCs melted into delocalized liquid-like states. This asymmetry arose from the broken particle-hole symmetry of the moiré superlattice, which produced electron and hole Fermi pockets with different momentum geometries upon GWC condensation. MI states melted without such asymmetry, consistent with the absence of a symmetry-breaking density modulation. This work provides direct visualization of the emergent phases that appear as GWCs undergo quantum melting transitions.

title: Sequential diagnosis with language models
abstract: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy on New England Journal of Medicine clinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.

title: Ultrarapid decision-making in an avian brain
abstract: Perceptual decision-making is well studied in mammals, but its operation in other vertebrates remains unclear. We show that carrion crows ( Corvus corone ) make deliberate decisions in a classic visual motion discrimination task with unprecedented speed, reporting choices in approximately 235 milliseconds on average, which is roughly twice as fast as has been observed in monkeys or humans and without sacrificing accuracy. Recordings from the pallial endbrain reveal that direction-selective neurons encode the upcoming choice as early as about 70 milliseconds after stimulus onset and about 170 milliseconds before the response, with ramping activity scaling with sensory evidence and converging at response onset. These findings highlight the extraordinary efficiency of avian decision-making circuitry, possibly shaped by evolutionary pressures for rapid visuomotor control.

title: “We’re Not Handling Cases, We’re Shaping Lives”: How Lawyers Preserve Professional Authority and Advance Social Responsibility via Moral Identity-Based Client Persuasion
abstract: Professionals are increasingly expected to deliver socially responsible services that protect vulnerable third parties, yet their authority may be threatened when such recommendations appear to conflict with clients’ perceived self-interests and desired end goals. Drawing on a qualitative study of 91 legal cases in China, we examine how lawyers navigate this tension when persuading initially resistant clients to accept socially responsible counsel. We develop a process model of “moral identity-based client persuasion,” a form of relational expertise that enables lawyers to preserve professional authority by reconstructing clients’ desired end goals to incorporate third-party welfare. The process begins with client moral identity discernment, through which lawyers determine whether a client’s moral identity is situationally salient. It unfolds through three linked practices: (1) articulating moral identity threats, (2) providing moral identity affirmations, and (3) legitimizing moral identity enactments. Together, these practices render socially responsible counsel both self-relevant and technically defensible to clients. We further identify three client-level inhibitors of success: insufficient moral identity salience, entangled decision locus, and limited emotional resilience. These findings augment research on professional work by identifying a novel form of relational expertise that mobilizes clients’ personal identities to secure compliance, and extend moral persuasion research into professional service contexts.

Information Transparency, Choice Confidence, and Customer Retention: Field and Laboratory Evidence from Markets for Credence Goods
abstract: How does information transparency affect customer retention in markets where quality is difficult to verify? Conventional wisdom suggests that transparency intensifies price competition and increases customer churn. We challenge this view by showing that acquisition-stage transparency can strengthen retention in markets for credence goods characterized by delayed feedback and persistent uncertainty, where customers revisit their decisions without clear quality signals. We develop a transparency-confidence-retention framework, in which transparency at acquisition builds choice confidence, a psychological switching cost that anchors customers to their initial decisions. Using 83,835 auto insurance contracts from a European insurer and multiple identification strategies, we find that customers acquired through transparent channels are 4.6%–11.8% less likely to churn than those acquired through less transparent channels. A randomized, controlled experiment with 1,515 participants shows that transparency reduces customer churn primarily by strengthening choice confidence rather than increasing conventional switching costs, such as brand trust or product fit. Decomposing transparency into attribute, comparative, and evaluative dimensions reveals that evaluative transparency exerts the strongest influence. Analyses of boundary conditions indicate that the retention effect of transparency is amplified when public and private signals remain congruent with earlier informational cues. These findings reconceptualize transparency as a relational mechanism that fosters decisional assurance and stabilizes retention under quality uncertainty. This paper was accepted by Anindya Ghose, information systems. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2020.02865 .

title: From Bytes to Bites: Examining the Online and Offline Spillover Impacts of Online Food Delivery Platform Subscriptions
abstract: With the rapid expansion of online food delivery (OFD) platforms, subscription models have emerged as a strategic tool to retain users and shape consumption behavior. Despite their growing prevalence, the broader impacts of these subscriptions—both within the OFD sector and across downstream consumer activities—remain underexplored. Leveraging a difference-in-differences approach and a large-scale individual-level transaction data set, we identify a significant shift in consumption from a competing platform to the focal platform following the introduction of a subscription service. This shift did not result in cannibalization; instead, overall food consumption within the OFD market increased. Geospatial analysis shows that subscribers were more likely to engage in offline spillovers, including increased local dining and activity in nearby noncompeting economic sectors. These patterns suggest that subscriptions in physical services, like OFD, not only reshape digital engagement, but also, they influence consumer mobility and stimulate localized economic ecosystems. Mechanistic testing supports the interpretation that these effects are driven by increased variety-seeking behavior for offline restaurants that predominantly serve non-OFD cuisines within a proximal location, suggesting that such behavior is constrained by transportation costs. Overall, this study offers novel insights into how subscription models in physical service platforms can expand market demand, foster crosschannel engagement, and generate positive spillovers in adjacent sectors. The findings offer actionable guidance for platform designers and policymakers to enhance consumer welfare and support local economic vitality. They also provide new evidence for restaurants that additional platform usage costs may be offset by latent economic benefits from heightened consumer engagement. This paper was accepted by D. J. Wu, information systems. Funding: F. J. Costello acknowledges funding by Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (UID/00124/2025, UID/ PRR/00124/2025, Nova School of Business and Economics DOI: https://doi.org/10.54499/UID/00124/2025 ), UID/PRR2/00124/2025: DOI: https://doi.org/10.54499/UID/PRR2/00124/2025 and LISBOA2030 (DataLab2030 - LISBOA2030-FEDER-01314200). Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.00954 .

title: From Winning to Giving: The Effect of Gold Medals in Crowdsourcing Contests
abstract: We examine how users respond to winning symbolic awards in online crowdsourcing contests. Our setting is a machine learning competition platform that grants symbolic medals to recognize participants’ contest achievements. Employing a regression discontinuity design, we find that gold medal winners participate less in subsequent contests but engage more in prosocial activities, evidenced by a greater volume and length of posts, as well as more substantial and frequent code contributions. In contrast, bronze and silver medals do not seem to exert a significant influence on recipients’ subsequent behaviors. Drawing on self-determination theory and the needs-as-motives hypothesis, we provide evidence that need-driven goal shifting plays an important role in driving the dual effects of gold medals—diminished contest participation but enhanced prosocial contributions. Further analyses reveal that winners with previous competition medals are more likely to favor contributing content over competing again, whereas winners with more prior contribution medals are less inclined to further increase contributions. Moreover, team winners exhibit a lower tendency than solo winners to shift their efforts from competition to contribution. We add to the symbolic awards literature by uncovering a novel goal-shifting effect induced by contest medals, where award receipt redirects user effort from the focal rewarded domain to other forms of platform engagement. This paper was accepted by D. J. Wu, information systems. Funding: Financial support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72032006, W2611101, and 72371192] and the “Digital-Intelligent Operations Risk Management” Innovation and Entrepreneurship Team Project of the Sanqin Talent Special Support Program in Shaanxi Province [2025STD03] is gratefully acknowledged. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.07419 .

title: Why Zoning Is Too Restrictive
abstract: Economists estimate that zoning regulations raise house prices, lower productivity, and reduce aggregate welfare, yet regulations remain widespread. We develop and solve a model in which fragmented zoning authority leads to overly strict regulations: Homeowners impose stricter regulations to mitigate local congestion but fail to internalize the broader impact on metro-wide affordability. Empirically, the Herfindahl-Hirschman index of local governments explains 12% of the variation in zoning restrictiveness. Using an instrument based on 19th-century municipal fragmentation, we show that greater fragmentation leads to stricter zoning and higher housing costs. These findings suggest that centralizing zoning decisions could alleviate housing affordability challenges. This paper was accepted by Lukas Schmid, finance. Funding: This work was supported by the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada [Grant AWD-027881 SSHRC 2023]. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.02844 .

title: Women’s Approachability Premium in Sales: A Field Experiment Among Microentrepreneurs
abstract: Female entrepreneurs consistently earn less than their male counterparts, a disparity that is particularly acute among microentrepreneurs in developing economies. Researchers often attribute this gap to structural constraints, but pay less attention to how social interactions shape earnings. This oversight is especially relevant in microentrepreneurship, where sales are contingent on customers approaching and interacting with sellers in the marketplace. Using an interactionist lens, we draw on social exchange theory and research on gender stereotypes to guide expectations. We anticipate that customers will more often approach female sellers, expecting warmer interactions, and that this higher volume will translate into higher earnings when business characteristics and selling behavior are held constant. Existing research hints at this dynamic, but methodological constraints have obscured it. To overcome these constraints and test our theory, we conducted a field experiment in two face-to-face markets in India. We trained confederate sellers to run identical, de novo microenterprises and follow standard protocols for customer engagement, thus isolating customer approach in response to sellers’ gender. Female sellers attracted 41% more customers, resulting in significantly higher sales than men, all else equal, in our experiment. Consistent with our theory, customers were more likely to talk with women about topics unrelated to the sale and attempt to bargain with women. This study advances research on gender dynamics in entrepreneurship, negotiation, and customer-facing work by identifying customer approach as a novel mechanism that can generate economic advantages for female microentrepreneurs and may shape gendered opportunities in other markets and organizations.

title: The Fragmentation of Material Flows: Mapping Barriers to Circular Economy Adoption in Bangladesh's Ready‐Made Garment Sector
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper provides an empirical diagnosis of the systemic challenges preventing the transition to a circular economy (CE) in Bangladesh's ready‐made garment (RMG) sector. Drawing on in‐depth interviews ( n = 13) with key industry stakeholders, the study characterises current waste flows and analyses the barriers to circularity. Findings reveal a predominantly linear material flow dominated by informal networks and constrained by a lack of traceability, limited recycling infrastructure and weak policy support. The study identifies power asymmetry between global brands and local manufacturers as one of four interacting ‘lock‐in’ mechanisms, alongside institutional voids, infrastructural and technological constraints and traceability failure, that together prevent the industry from moving beyond fragmented, linear practices. This structural governance failure actively inhibits progress toward Sustainable Development Goal 12, particularly Targets 12.5 and 12.6. Based on the multilevel perspective, supplemented by institutional theory and the resource‐based view, the analysis argues that the current linear production regime is maintained by institutional voids and internal resource constraints that must be addressed before prescriptive solutions can be operationalised. The empirical scope centres on postproduction and preconsumer waste governance; postconsumer textile waste is examined specifically as an import‐ and feedstock‐classification barrier rather than as an empirically traced material flow.

title: Circular Economy Practices and Sustainable Performance: An Empirical Study
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the extent to which basic and advanced circular economy practices are associated in different ways with the environmental, economic and social dimensions of sustainable performance at the firm level. Starting from the premise that the circular economy should not be treated as a homogeneous construct, the study distinguishes between more operational practices, geared towards efficiency and waste reduction, and more transformational practices, associated with redesign, value retention and the reconfiguration of value creation and capture models. Empirically, a quantitative, cross‐sectional, organisation‐level design is adopted, based on 255 companies operating in Portugal. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics, reliability tests, bivariate correlations and hierarchical ordinary least squares regressions. The results show that basic circular economy practices exhibit positive, robust and consistent associations with environmental performance and economic performance, emerging as the empirically strongest core of circular value creation. The environmental dimension proves to be the aspect of sustainable performance most directly sensitive to the adoption of these practices. In contrast, although advanced practices show positive associations in intermediate models, they do not demonstrate a robust incremental contribution to economic and social performance in the full models. The study contributes to the literature by emphasising the need to distinguish between different types of circular practices, by linking the debate on the circular economy to the literature on strategy and sustainability and by offering a more nuanced understanding of multidimensional sustainable performance. In practical terms, the findings suggest that organisations should not assume that more advanced circular practices automatically generate stronger performance outcomes and that the contribution of different forms of circularity should be assessed in relation to their specific organisational and performance context.

title: Reframing Stakeholder Roles in Multistakeholder Partnerships: A Role Theory Approach to Collaborative Action on Food Waste
abstract: ABSTRACT Multistakeholder partnerships (MSPs) are promoted as collaborative arrangements to address food waste, yet most research focuses on core stakeholders directly involved in food production and consumption, leaving the roles of supporting stakeholders underexplored. This study redirects attention to these vital actors, such as governmental bodies, financial institutions, and industry associations, whose engagement can be important to initiating, stabilizing, and sustaining collaboration. Drawing on role theory, we examine the case of Food Waste Free United in the Netherlands through interviews and secondary data. We identify four dynamic role orientations enacted by supporting stakeholders: mediator, facilitator, supporter, and influencer. Each role embodies distinct practices, ranging from building trust and establishing data sharing arrangements to mobilizing networks, shaping policy, and strengthening capabilities, which can contribute to the stability and effectiveness of MSPs. Our analysis further reveals that motivations to engage extend beyond external pressure, encompassing a search for embeddedness within the partnership ecosystem and opportunities for learning. By applying role theory, we advance understanding of how supporting stakeholders enable MSPs to move beyond fragile arrangements toward sustained, systemic impact. These insights offer theoretical contributions to stakeholder and role theory that, in turn, inform practical guidance for designing partnerships that more effectively integrate diverse actors in the fight against food waste.

title: Institutional technologies and the new frontiers of international marketing and global supply chain management
abstract: Purpose This paper introduces the concept of institutional technologies as the socio-technical and interorganizational mechanisms and practices that enable the governance and coordination of economic exchange. We argue that emerging institutional technologies, such as digital platforms, distributed ledgers, smart contracts and digital traceability systems, are reshaping the foundations of international marketing and global supply chain management (SCM) by changing how firms create, substantiate and deliver value across borders. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on a conceptual and integrative approach, this paper examines how emerging institutional technologies alter the conditions under which firms create, substantiate and deliver value propositions and engage in economic exchange. We develop a framework that links institutional technologies to the governance, accountability and legitimacy processes that shape the international marketing–global SCM interface. Findings We argue that institutional technologies are reordering coordination, accountability, legitimacy and value capture across borders. We further suggest that the international marketing–global SCM interface has become a site of joint institutional work, where firms shape technology-enabled standards, proofs and governance arrangements that underpin contemporary cross-border exchange. Building on this perspective, this paper proposes five directions for future research: traceability as a market promise; platformization of international marketing; automation and smart contracts in relation to relational repair; algorithmic coordination as institutional technology; and the interplay between institutional technologies, regulation, geopolitics and infrastructures. We develop five propositions that link each cluster of institutional technologies to the forms of institutional work it performs, the outcomes it influences and the institutional conditions that shape these relationships. Originality/value This paper advances a more technologically grounded understanding of the interface between international marketing and global SCM. It offers a novel conceptual foundation for examining how the technological architectures and governance models of cross-border exchange are being fundamentally recast.
